# Task 35: macOS .app bundle wrapping so the keychain entitlement actually works

## Overview
Task_33 landed the codesigning + entitlement + notarization infrastructure with the understanding (per ADR-023) that AMFI would read the embedded provisioning profile from a Mach-O `__TEXT,__provisioning` section. Empirical investigation on 2026-06-19 against macOS 26.2 proved that recipe is folklore — AMFI doesn't look at that section. The canonical Apple path is to wrap the binaries inside a `.app` bundle with `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` as a file. ADR-025 captures the finding + decision. This task carries the implementation work to switch from raw Mach-O CLIs to a single FFS.app bundle wrapping all three binaries, then validates end-to-end that the keychain path finally works (task_27's empirical close).

<critical>
- ALWAYS READ the PRD and TechSpec before starting
- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here
- FOCUS ON "WHAT" — describe what needs to be accomplished, not how
- MINIMIZE CODE — show code only to illustrate current structure or problem areas
- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

<requirements>
- MUST emit a `FFS.app` bundle as the macOS release artifact, structured per ADR-025: `Contents/Info.plist` + `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` + `Contents/MacOS/{ffs,ffs-daemon,ffs-mcp}` + `Contents/_CodeSignature/`. CFBundleIdentifier matches the bundle ID the provisioning profile authorizes; `LSUIElement=true` so the bundle stays headless.
- MUST delete the per-crate `build.rs` files added in commit `2be3b5a`. Their `-Wl,-sectcreate` linker args are no-ops AMFI never reads; keeping them around is misleading and they break the FFS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE env-var contract (the env var becomes irrelevant because the profile is a file in the bundle, not a section in the binary).
- MUST rewrite `scripts/codesign-macos.sh` to: (1) construct the bundle from the just-built release binaries, (2) place `embedded.provisionprofile` + `Info.plist` at `Contents/`, (3) `codesign --force --deep --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements … --sign … FFS.app`. The current per-Mach-O sign loop goes away. The script's existing argument shape can stay (binaries listed positionally) so the CI workflow doesn't need to know about the bundle structure.
- MUST update `installer/install.sh` to: (1) place `FFS.app` under `~/.local/Applications/FFS.app` (or `/Applications/FFS.app` for system installs), (2) create symlinks at `~/.local/bin/{ffs,ffs-daemon,ffs-mcp}` pointing into `Contents/MacOS/`, (3) clean up old install paths if upgrading from a pre-task_35 install (`~/.local/bin/ffs-daemon` may previously have been a regular file, not a symlink).
- MUST update `installer/launchd/com.ffs.daemon.plist` so `ProgramArguments` points at the bundle's internal daemon path. Symlinks would break under launchd's plist resolution; the absolute bundle path is the correct shape.
- MUST update `.github/workflows/release.yml` to produce a single `FFS.app.zip` release artifact (one zip per macOS arch — x86_64 + aarch64), submit to `notarytool` as the bundle, and `xcrun stapler staple FFS.app` so the ticket is attached to the bundle directly. Stapling works on bundles where it didn't work for raw Mach-O.
- MUST update the integration test override (`FFS_SIGNED_DAEMON_BIN` in `tests/sqlite_persistence.rs`) so it accepts either a bundle path (`…/FFS.app/Contents/MacOS/ffs-daemon`) or a raw binary path. Today the test code is already shape-agnostic since it just passes the path to `Command::new`, but the docs around `FFS_SIGNED_DAEMON_BIN` need to clarify the bundle case.
- MUST update ADR-023 to add a "Superseded for implementation by ADR-025" pointer in its references section. The intent (use access groups + codesigning + notarization) is upheld; only the section-embed mechanism is corrected.
- MUST update `docs/onboarding/technical-friend-checklist.md` Step 2 Path B with the corrected build → bundle → sign → notarize → staple recipe. Drop the `FFS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE` env var references (the env var no longer exists because build.rs is gone).
- MUST update `docs/onboarding/troubleshooting.md` keychain section with the three-gate diagnostic shape adapted to bundle paths: `codesign -d --entitlements - FFS.app`, `xcrun stapler validate FFS.app`, and a path check that the daemon binary symlink resolves into a bundle.
- SHOULD verify the bundle works under launchd by loading the daemon plist on the project lead's Mac and confirming `ffs identity show` reports `source: keychain` AND the pubkey stays stable across two consecutive boots. This is the empirical close of task_27 we've been chasing.
- SHOULD test the same on a second Apple architecture if available (x86_64 in Rosetta or aarch64 native), to make sure the bundle layout works on both. The CI release matrix already produces both, so the CI green is partial proof.
</requirements>

# Task 35: macOS .app bundle wrapping so the keychain entitlement actually works

## Overview
Task_33 landed the codesigning + entitlement + notarization infrastructure with the understanding (per ADR-023) that AMFI would read the embedded provisioning profile from a Mach-O `__TEXT,__provisioning` section. Empirical investigation on 2026-06-19 against macOS 26.2 proved that recipe is folklore — AMFI doesn't look at that section. The canonical Apple path is to wrap the binaries inside a `.app` bundle with `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` as a file. ADR-025 captures the finding + decision. This task carries the implementation work to switch from raw Mach-O CLIs to a single FFS.app bundle wrapping all three binaries, then validates end-to-end that the keychain path finally works (task_27's empirical close).

<critical>
- ALWAYS READ the PRD and TechSpec before starting
- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here
- FOCUS ON "WHAT" — describe what needs to be accomplished, not how
- MINIMIZE CODE — show code only to illustrate current structure or problem areas
- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

<requirements>
- MUST emit a `FFS.app` bundle as the macOS release artifact, structured per ADR-025: `Contents/Info.plist` + `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` + `Contents/MacOS/{ffs,ffs-daemon,ffs-mcp}` + `Contents/_CodeSignature/`. CFBundleIdentifier matches the bundle ID the provisioning profile authorizes; `LSUIElement=true` so the bundle stays headless.
- MUST delete the per-crate `build.rs` files added in commit `2be3b5a`. Their `-Wl,-sectcreate` linker args are no-ops AMFI never reads; keeping them around is misleading and they break the FFS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE env-var contract (the env var becomes irrelevant because the profile is a file in the bundle, not a section in the binary).
- MUST rewrite `scripts/codesign-macos.sh` to: (1) construct the bundle from the just-built release binaries, (2) place `embedded.provisionprofile` + `Info.plist` at `Contents/`, (3) `codesign --force --deep --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements … --sign … FFS.app`. The current per-Mach-O sign loop goes away. The script's existing argument shape can stay (binaries listed positionally) so the CI workflow doesn't need to know about the bundle structure.
- MUST update `installer/install.sh` to: (1) place `FFS.app` under `~/.local/Applications/FFS.app` (or `/Applications/FFS.app` for system installs), (2) create symlinks at `~/.local/bin/{ffs,ffs-daemon,ffs-mcp}` pointing into `Contents/MacOS/`, (3) clean up old install paths if upgrading from a pre-task_35 install (`~/.local/bin/ffs-daemon` may previously have been a regular file, not a symlink).
- MUST update `installer/launchd/com.ffs.daemon.plist` so `ProgramArguments` points at the bundle's internal daemon path. Symlinks would break under launchd's plist resolution; the absolute bundle path is the correct shape.
- MUST update `.github/workflows/release.yml` to produce a single `FFS.app.zip` release artifact (one zip per macOS arch — x86_64 + aarch64), submit to `notarytool` as the bundle, and `xcrun stapler staple FFS.app` so the ticket is attached to the bundle directly. Stapling works on bundles where it didn't work for raw Mach-O.
- MUST update the integration test override (`FFS_SIGNED_DAEMON_BIN` in `tests/sqlite_persistence.rs`) so it accepts either a bundle path (`…/FFS.app/Contents/MacOS/ffs-daemon`) or a raw binary path. Today the test code is already shape-agnostic since it just passes the path to `Command::new`, but the docs around `FFS_SIGNED_DAEMON_BIN` need to clarify the bundle case.
- MUST update ADR-023 to add a "Superseded for implementation by ADR-025" pointer in its references section. The intent (use access groups + codesigning + notarization) is upheld; only the section-embed mechanism is corrected.
- MUST update `docs/onboarding/technical-friend-checklist.md` Step 2 Path B with the corrected build → bundle → sign → notarize → staple recipe. Drop the `FFS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE` env var references (the env var no longer exists because build.rs is gone).
- MUST update `docs/onboarding/troubleshooting.md` keychain section with the three-gate diagnostic shape adapted to bundle paths: `codesign -d --entitlements - FFS.app`, `xcrun stapler validate FFS.app`, and a path check that the daemon binary symlink resolves into a bundle.
- SHOULD verify the bundle works under launchd by loading the daemon plist on the project lead's Mac and confirming `ffs identity show` reports `source: keychain` AND the pubkey stays stable across two consecutive boots. This is the empirical close of task_27 we've been chasing.
- SHOULD test the same on a second Apple architecture if available (x86_64 in Rosetta or aarch64 native), to make sure the bundle layout works on both. The CI release matrix already produces both, so the CI green is partial proof.
</requirements>

The MCP tool set after ADR-027 is eight tools: ffs_query, ffs_search (new: entity.search by name/title, params query + limit ≤50, returns lightweight hits entity/predicate/display_name), ffs_list_path (new: path.list over a projection listing such as contacts/by-name/S/ or notes/recent/, params path + optional page), ffs_render_projection, ffs_resolve_url, ffs_author_atom (submits content to the ingest quarantine; returns a submission_id for a PROPOSAL, nothing persisted until the user accepts), ffs_inspect_predicate, ffs_audit_query.

Write:

1. docs/agent-memory/CONVENTION.md — "FFS Agent Memory Convention v0.1". Structure it like the OKF convention (numbered sections, MUST/SHOULD language) but FFS-native. Required sections: Purpose; Relationship to the OKF Agent Memory Convention (credit it explicitly: this is an adaptation of okf-memory/okf-agent-memory's convention onto a records-shaped substrate; the OKF file format is NOT adopted because FFS atoms already carry richer provenance/lifecycle; link https://github.com/okf-memory/okf-agent-memory); Design principles (persistent knowledge survives conversations; the substrate is the long-term state, not a transcript; prefer existing over duplication; preserve uncertainty; human gate); a mapping table "OKF concept → FFS primitive" (concept→entity+predicate atoms; type→predicate; description→display_name/title; generated.by→atom author key + provenance kind; verified→user acceptance from quarantine (proposal is 'generated', accepted atom signed by the owner is 'verified'); sources→provenance entries; status/stale_after→valid_from/valid_to bitemporal window + supersession; relationships→claim references/`references` field and entity links; index.md→projection listings via ffs_list_path; log.md→tx_time ordering + audit.query; governance/code_refs→capability atoms (for the app) and the ADR governance index (for the repo)); What to remember / what not to; Knowledge lifecycle (Discover→Evaluate→Search (ffs_search)→Propose or extend (ffs_author_atom)→Provenance→Await human acceptance→Revisit); Read-before-write sequence; Progressive disclosure (ffs_list_path/ffs_search → ffs_render_projection/ffs_query → ffs_resolve_url only for what's needed; never dump the substrate; respect limits); Provenance and trust (never claim human verification; proposals are not atoms; engine/model provenance per ADR-026); Inference ("Based on A and B, the agent infers C" goes in the content); Conflicts and supersession (never silently overwrite; supersession preserves history; the user disambiguates multi-leaf heads); Human override (a rejected proposal MUST NOT be re-proposed without new evidence; the daily summary is the fence); Capability boundary (a capability denial is the substrate's answer, not an error to route around); Failure handling / persistence honesty (report submission_id as proposed; never say saved); Minimal Agent Contract (10–11 numbered rules, FFS flavored); Open questions (full-text search over claim bodies, MCP-side supersede, agent-authored capability requests, stale-detection via auditor). Keep it around 250–350 lines. Plain prose, no em-dashes.

2. docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-memory/SKILL.md — an installable agent skill with YAML frontmatter `name: ffs-memory` and a `description:` that triggers whenever an agent should persist or recall knowledge through FFS. Body: Minimal Agent Contract; Tooling reference table (MCP tool preferred → `ffs` CLI fallback: `ffs ls <path>`, `ffs cat <path>`, `ffs get ffs://...` — check crates/ffs-cli/src/commands.rs for the actual CLI verbs and only cite ones that exist); Workflow: discover (ffs_search/ffs_list_path), inspect, propose (ffs_author_atom content shape: markdown with frontmatter matching a predicate; cite ffs_inspect_predicate), report honestly; End-of-task knowledge review checklist. Explain in docs/agent-memory/README.md how to install the skill: copy or symlink the `ffs-memory` directory into `.claude/skills/` (Claude Code) or `.agents/skills/` (claw hosts), and the ffs-mcp `mcpServers` block (copy the exact block from README.md). Note this skill is instructional only and is NOT a daemon-hosted skill bundle (no entry_point; do not put it under skills/, the skills host would reject it).

3. Onboarding pointers: in docs/onboarding/technical-friend-checklist.md, find the step where ffs-mcp / MCP configuration is described (grep for mcp) and add 2–3 lines pointing to docs/agent-memory/README.md for the convention + skill. In docs/onboarding/first-use-guide.md "What now?" section add one bullet: if you point an AI agent at FFS, it should follow the Agent Memory Convention (link). Keep both edits minimal and in the existing voice.

Do not commit. Report the files created/edited and a 5-line summary of the convention's contract.

1	//! The eight MCP tools: the six MVP tools per ADR-013 plus
2	//! `ffs_search` and `ffs_list_path` per ADR-027 (the FFS Agent Memory
3	//! Convention — search-before-write and progressive disclosure need
4	//! a lightweight search + listing surface). Each tool exposes:
5	//!
6	//! - A `name` matching ADR-013 (`ffs_query`, `ffs_render_projection`,
7	//!   `ffs_resolve_url`, `ffs_author_atom`, `ffs_inspect_predicate`,
8	//!   `ffs_audit_query`) or ADR-027 (`ffs_search`, `ffs_list_path`).
9	//! - A JSON Schema `inputSchema` so MCP-aware clients can validate
10	//!   arguments before the call.
11	//! - A translator that turns the MCP `arguments` object into the
12	//!   matching daemon JSON-RPC method + params and shapes the
13	//!   response back into an MCP `ToolCallResult`.
14	//!
15	//! Capability checks happen entirely on the daemon side (ADR-013) —
16	//! the MCP server is a thin pass-through. `DaemonError::CapabilityDenied`
17	//! comes back as a tool-level error with `isError: true`, the
18	//! canonical MCP shape for "the agent's request was authenticated
19	//! and well-formed, but the substrate refused it".
20	
21	use serde_json::Value;
22	
23	use crate::daemon_client::{DaemonClient, DaemonError};
24	use crate::protocol::{Tool, ToolCallResult};
25	
26	/// Default hit count for `ffs_search` when the agent omits `limit`.
27	/// Small on purpose: the convention (ADR-027) wants agents to read a
28	/// handful of lightweight hits and drill in, not page through the
29	/// substrate.
30	pub const SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT: u64 = 10;
31	/// Hard ceiling for `ffs_search` `limit` — larger requests are clamped.
32	pub const SEARCH_MAX_LIMIT: u64 = 50;
33	
34	/// Build the eight-tool catalog the MCP server advertises on
35	/// `tools/list`. The JSON Schemas are intentionally tolerant — most
36	/// fields are optional so an agent can call a tool with the

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, indefinitely** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Timeout → killed. Set `persistent: true` for session-length watches (PR monitoring, log tails) — the monitor runs until you call TaskStop or the session ends. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms, max 3600000ms. Ignored when persistent is true.

persistent.description: Run for the lifetime of the session (no timeout). Use for session-length watches like PR monitoring or log tails. Stop with TaskStop.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

190	### Pre-1.0 stability
191	
192	The project is pre-1.0. Breaking changes are possible everywhere with notice. Post-1.0, the stable surfaces listed in [`ARCHITECTURE.md` § Stability commitments](ARCHITECTURE.md#stability-commitments) lock down (`ffs://` URL scheme, atom envelope shape, JSON-RPC method set, MCP tool signatures, predicate-spec format).
193	
194	Until 1.0, prefer breaking change + clear migration over backward-compatibility hacks. After 1.0, prefer additive change over breaking change.
195	
196	---
197	
198	## Knowledge discipline (ADR-027)
199	
200	This repo's persistent memory is `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the ADRs, and the task files under `.compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/` — not the chat. A future session has none of this conversation; anything it would otherwise have to rediscover belongs in one of those three places. The practice is adopted from [okf-agent-memory](https://github.com/okf-memory/okf-agent-memory) per [ADR-027](.compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/adrs/adr-027.md).
201	
202	**Read before write.** Before substantial work under a path, open [`.compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/adrs/README.md`](.compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/adrs/README.md) and read the ADRs listed for that path. Respect the tier: `constraint` binds the edit; `hold` means stop and ask the user before touching the path; `context` is background. Search the existing ADRs and task files before proposing a new one — prefer updating an ADR's Implementation Notes or a task's Overview over creating a near-duplicate.
203	
204	**Progressive disclosure.** Use the ADR index and `Grep` to find the one or two ADRs a task needs. Do not read all 27 ADRs to answer a question one row of the index answers.
205	
206	**End-of-task knowledge review.** Before declaring a task done, ask:
207	
208	- Did I make a decision that changes a public type, the atom envelope, the capability evaluator, federation transport, the MCP tool set, or any stability-commitment surface? → new ADR (sequential number), plus a row or an added reference in the governance index.
209	- Did I change an invariant, a concurrency rule, or a component boundary? → update `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
210	- Did I discover something non-obvious (a folklore fix that doesn't work, a platform quirk, a failure mode)? → record it in the task file's Overview or the relevant ADR's Implementation Notes, the way ADR-023/025 and task_36 do.
211	- Did nothing above apply? → write nothing. Do not manufacture a low-value entry to have something to show.
212	
213	**Persistence honesty.** Never report an ADR, doc, or task file as written unless it exists on disk — verify with `ls` or `Read` before claiming it. Never flip an ADR to `Accepted` or a task to `completed` on the user's behalf when the work was only proposed or partially delivered. The same rule the substrate enforces on agents (a quarantined proposal is not a saved atom) applies to us and the repo's own memory.
214	
215	---
216	
217	## Verification before completion claims
218	
219	Every "task complete", "tests pass", "ready to commit" claim requires fresh verification evidence. The full template lives in the `cy-final-verify` skill; the short form is:
220

# ADR governance index

This index binds code paths to the architecture decision records that govern them, in the manner of okf-agent-memory's `code_refs` + `governance` practice (ADR-027). It is the repo's "what governs this file?" lookup and the one-sentence-description layer for progressive disclosure: read this table, then open only the ADRs the task actually touches.

## Tiers

| Tier | Meaning for an agent or contributor editing the referenced paths |
|---|---|
| **constraint** | Mandatory guardrail. You may edit the code, but the ADR's decision binds the edit. A change that contradicts the ADR needs a new ADR that supersedes it first. |
| **hold** | Execution freeze. Do not modify the referenced paths without explicit human approval in the current session. |
| **context** | Advisory background. Read it to understand why the code is shaped the way it is; it does not gate the edit. |

**How to use:** before substantial work under a path, find its row below and read the governing ADRs. Respect the tier. If a path is not listed, `ARCHITECTURE.md` is the governing document and the tier is `constraint` for anything under § Invariants or § Stability commitments.

## Active holds

No active holds.

## Path → governing ADRs → tier

| Path(s) | Governing ADRs | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ffs-core/src/atom.rs`, `crates/ffs-core/src/multihash.rs`, `crates/ffs-core/src/multibase.rs` | ADR-017 (JCS envelope, `v` field is the migration knob), ADR-018 (Ed25519 / BLAKE3 / multibase), ADR-001 (records, not files) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/capability/` | ADR-007 (personal federation, capability atoms), ADR-013 (capability checks at the MCP boundary delegate here), ADR-020 (source-side evaluation for federation pulls) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/predicate/`, `starter/predicates/` | ADR-021 (TOML + embedded JSON Schema spec format), ADR-014 (reverse-map annotations feed the fast-path) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/projection/`, `crates/ffs-core/src/working_set.rs`, `starter/templates/` | ADR-005 (editor-agnostic materialized working set), ADR-011 (three path families), ADR-014 (reverse-map-annotated output) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/store/` (`sqlite.rs`, `schema.rs`, `migrations.rs`, `mem.rs`) | ADR-016 (single SQLite DB per substrate, normalized schema, SQLCipher) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/store/keyring.rs`, `crates/ffs-core/src/store/keyring_macos.rs` | ADR-023 (keychain access group; intent upheld), ADR-025 (profile delivery via `.app` bundle) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/quarantine.rs`, `crates/ffs-core/src/quarantine_sqlite.rs` | ADR-013 (proposal quarantine as the human gate for agent writes), ADR-027 (proposal ≠ persisted; agents report "proposed") | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-core/src/suppress.rs`, `crates/ffs-fastpath/` | ADR-014 (minimum-viable fast-path scope), ADR-005 (edits from any editor route to atoms or ingest) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-daemon/src/` | ADR-015 (minimal Rust daemon), ADR-019 (UDS / named pipe + JSON-RPC 2.0 method set), ADR-022 (`$FFS_DATA_DIR` is the vault root), ADR-024 (no Windows ACL code in the daemon), ADR-025 (daemon is the only binary inside `FFS.app`) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-daemon/src/scribe.rs`, `crates/ffs-daemon/src/ingest_watcher.rs` | ADR-026 (scribe v2 engine seam; provenance carries engine + model), ADR-009 (stdlib-only skill bundles) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-cli/` | ADR-006 (`ffs://` scheme is a stable noun, three address modes), ADR-019 (same JSON-RPC client as the plugin and MCP server) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-federation/` | ADR-020 (mTLS over HTTPS, pull-based, fingerprint-pinned), ADR-007 (bilateral personal federation), ADR-012 (pairwise only; no multi-peer aggregation), ADR-018 (cert from the Ed25519 key) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-mcp/` | ADR-013 (thin pass-through; capability checks on the daemon side), ADR-008 (speak MCP at the boundary), ADR-027 (eight-tool catalog; `ffs_search`, `ffs_list_path`, proposal wording), ADR-006 (`ffs_resolve_url` address modes) | constraint |
| `crates/ffs-skills-host/`, `skills/` | ADR-009 (`SKILL.md`-shaped, claw-portable, zero pip deps), ADR-026 (extraction engines live inside the scribe bundle), ADR-015 (subprocess + stdio hosting) | constraint |
| `obsidian-plugin/` | ADR-005 (plugin is one editor among many; substrate is canonical), ADR-022 (vault root = `$FFS_DATA_DIR`), ADR-019 (UDS / named-pipe client) | constraint |
| `installer/`, `bundle/`, `entitlements/`, `scripts/codesign-macos.sh`, `.github/workflows/release.yml` | ADR-022 (installer seeds `$FFS_DATA_DIR/.obsidian/`), ADR-023 (Developer ID signing + notarization intent), ADR-024 (`icacls` at install time on Windows), ADR-025 (`FFS.app` wraps only the daemon) | constraint |
| `docs/agent-memory/` | ADR-027 (the FFS Agent Memory Convention and the `ffs-memory` skill) | constraint |
| `docs/onboarding/` | ADR-022 (open `~/.ffs/` as the vault), ADR-025 (bundle-aware install and diagnostics), ADR-026 (engine configuration and privacy posture) | context |
| `.compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/adrs/` (this directory) | `CLAUDE.md` § ADRs (numbering, when a new ADR is required), ADR-027 (keep this index current) | context |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md` | ADR-001 through ADR-004 (product shape), ADR-013 and ADR-027 (MCP surface described there) | context |

## All ADRs, one line each

| ADR | Status | One sentence |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-001](adr-001.md) | Accepted | FFS is records-shaped: the substrate stores signed, classified atoms; files are surfaces only. |
| [ADR-002](adr-002.md) | Accepted | Developers and end users are both first-class audiences; neither surface is deferred. |
| [ADR-003](adr-003.md) | Accepted | Substrate-first MVP: ship the primitives with functional-not-polished surfaces and validate with a small community. |
| [ADR-004](adr-004.md) | Accepted | All three motivating scenarios (contact sovereignty, home-claw absorption, clone-and-collaborate) ship in MVP. |
| [ADR-005](adr-005.md) | Accepted | Projections are a materialized working set of real files any editor can open; no kernel driver, no Obsidian lock-in. |
| [ADR-006](adr-006.md) | Accepted | `ffs://<graph>/<address>` is a public, stable URL scheme with path, atom, and entity address modes. |
| [ADR-007](adr-007.md) | Accepted | MVP ships personal (bilateral, capability-atom) federation; organizational federation is Phase 3. |
| [ADR-008](adr-008.md) | Accepted | Speak MCP and A2A at boundaries; FFS-native semantics between FFS substrates. |
| [ADR-009](adr-009.md) | Accepted | FFS agents are `SKILL.md`-shaped, claw-portable, stdlib-only bundles; FFS does not reimplement the claw. |
| [ADR-010](adr-010.md) | Superseded by ADR-013 | Original deferral of the MCP server to Phase 2; kept for the historical record. |
| [ADR-011](adr-011.md) | Accepted | The path library starts at three families: `contacts/`, `people/`, `notes/`. |
| [ADR-012](adr-012.md) | Accepted | Federation is pairwise in MVP; multi-peer aggregation is Phase 2. |
| [ADR-013](adr-013.md) | Accepted (supersedes ADR-010) | The MCP server is MVP with six tools; capability checks are delegated to the daemon's evaluator. |

content.content:
## 5. Mapping OKF Concepts to FFS Primitives

| OKF concept | FFS primitive |
|---|---|
| Concept (one `.md` file) | An entity: the head atoms across its predicates |
| `type` | The predicate name (`contact.person`, `note`, `person.generic`, any registered predicate) |
| `description` (one sentence) | The predicate's canonical name field: `display_name` or `title` |
| `generated: { by, at }` | The atom's `author` public key, plus a `provenance` entry with `kind: mcp_agent` or `ingest_file` and the source URI |
| `verified: [ human ]` | Owner acceptance from the quarantine. A proposal is "generated". An accepted atom is signed by the owner's key and is "verified" |
| `sources` | `provenance` entries (`kind`, `uri`, `hash`) on the atom |
| `status`, `stale_after` | The bitemporal window (`valid_from`, `valid_to`) and the supersession chain; a superseded atom is history, not deleted |
| Relationships (Markdown links) | The `references` field on notes, entity ids in claims, and the `History` and `Notes` sections of contacts |
| `index.md` progressive disclosure | Projection listings read through `ffs_list_path` (`contacts/by-name/S/`, `notes/recent/`) |
| `log.md` dated history | `tx_time` ordering on atoms and `ffs_audit_query` over auditor daily summaries |
| `governance` and `code_refs` | For the substrate: capability atoms, evaluated at every call. For the FFS repository itself: the ADR governance index described in ADR-027 |
| `okf validate` | Predicate claim-schema validation at ingest and at accept; the auditor's daily summary for drift |

The mapping is intentionally lossy in one direction: FFS records who signed each claim and when the substrate received it, which OKF does not require. Agents SHOULD lean on that extra structure instead of re-encoding provenance in prose.

---

## 6. What Should Be Remembered
=====
## 18. Minimal Agent Contract

Any agent using FFS as memory MUST understand this contract:

1. Persistent knowledge belongs in the substrate, proposed through `ffs_author_atom` or `~/.ffs/ingest/`.
2. Search before proposing (`ffs_search`).
3. Read listings and projections before atoms; never dump the substrate.
4. Extend existing entities rather than creating near-duplicates.
5. Do not propose conversation, reasoning, or transient state.
6. Set `source_uri` to the real origin when there is one.
7. Mark inferences as inferences in the content.
8. Never overwrite; supersession preserves history, and the owner resolves conflicts.
9. Never re-propose what the owner rejected without new evidence.
10. A capability denial is the answer; do not route around it.
11. A `submission_id` means proposed, not saved. Never claim persistence that did not happen.

---

content.text:
Honest answer: the Mac Mini half is ready, the pipeline you describe is not. Three of its six stages work today, and the three that don't are design gaps, not bugs.

**What works now on a Mac Mini**

- **Daemon on launchd with keychain identity.** Task 35 closed with live launchd validation. You need the Developer ID signed `FFS.app` bundle for the keychain path; an unsigned local build falls back to env-var keys and still runs.
- **Ingest to vault.** Anything an agent writes as markdown into `~/.ffs/ingest/` waits out the 30-second stability window, gets scribed into quarantine, and once accepted is materialized into `~/.ffs/`, which is the Obsidian vault. That "radiation" step is real and tested.
- **Agent interface.** Hermes only needs to do one of two things FFS supports: write files into the ingest folder, or call the eight `ffs-mcp` tools. The convention and skill from yesterday tell it how.

**What does not work yet**

1. **"Automatically" is against the design.** Every proposal requires a human accept in the daily summary. The only accept path is the plugin calling `ingest.accept` by hand, and ARCHITECTURE.md lists batch approval as an anti-pattern. A nightly CBJ digest with 30 links means 30 or more cards to review each morning. Auto-accepting a trusted agent within a predicate scope would be a new capability-gated flow and needs an ADR.
2. **The scribe cannot build a business graph.** Task 36 (schema-driven LLM extraction) is still pending. The shipped scribe is the regex engine that produced "Bones Occupation". Fed a CBJ article, it will emit a `note` proposal and, at best, mangled person names. It will never produce an organization, a role, or a deal.
3. **There are no business predicates.** The path library is contacts, people, and notes. A local business graph needs at least `org.company`, `person.role` or affiliation, and some event or deal predicate, each as a TOML spec plus a Tera template. Adding them is supported, but extraction into them depends on item 2.
4. **No graph queries or full-text search.** `ffs_search` matches names and titles only, and the starter templates emit no wikilinks, so Obsidian's graph view would show nothing connected. "Up-to-date understanding" would come from reading rendered notes, not from traversing a graph.

**Outside FFS entirely**

- **Email intake, logged-in browsing, and link-clicking** are Hermes's job. FFS has never been run inside Hermes or OpenClaw. ADR-009 made that claw integration an operational choice, and the MVP built the minimal daemon path instead. Expect to write the Hermes-side skill yourself.
- **Credentials and terms of use.** Scraping a paywalled publication with your session is your call, but it is the riskiest part of the plan and none of it touches FFS.

**Order I would build in**

1. Finish task 36 with the Anthropic or Ollama engine, since nothing downstream is useful without real extraction.
2. Add three business predicates and templates, with wikilinks in the templates so the vault graph lights up.
3. Decide on an auto-accept capability for a named agent and predicate scope, with an ADR, or accept the morning review as the feature.
4. Then wire Hermes to drop markdown per article into the ingest folder and start with one email.

If you want, I can scope steps 1 through 3 as tasks 38 to 40 in the plan.

content.text:
Agreed on both, and the code confirms they're needed: path families are a hardcoded three-variant enum, `ffs_search` matches only the name field, and no template emits a wikilink. Here is the design I'm committing to before writing the tasks. Forks will write the files from this block.

**The newspaper frame, translated**

- **Reading end-to-end** = one `source.article` record per article (title, publication, url, published_at, byline, agent-written summary, `mentions` of people and orgs, tags) plus one daily `note` digest listing everything read. No full text is stored; the URL is the provenance anchor, the summary is the memory.
- **Filing cabinets** = four drawers: `people/` (person.generic v2: adds organization, aliases, mentions history), `orgs/` (new `org.company`), `events/` (new `event.business`: kind enum such as funding, acquisition, hire, expansion, opening, closing, award; date, parties, amount, summary), `articles/` (new `source.article`). `contacts/` stays for people you actually know.
- **Cross-references** = wikilinks emitted by templates (a person's org renders as `[[Org]]`, an article's mentions link to people and orgs), so Obsidian's graph view becomes the business graph.
- **The clerk** = scribe v2 (task_36, amended): one article yields the article record plus N person, M org, and K event proposals with cross-refs, and proposals are resolved against existing entities so a repeat mention updates a file instead of opening a duplicate.
- **Filing policy** = capability-gated auto-file (ADR-029): a named agent may auto-accept additive proposals (new entity, appended history) in scoped predicates; anything that would overwrite an existing scalar (a role change) always goes to your review. The daily summary shows what was auto-filed with an undo.
- **What we do next** = a morning briefing from the auditor: people newly seen or moved, orgs trending, `person.generic` records mentioned often enough to promote to contacts, follow-up suggestions.

**Not FFS**: fetching the email, logged-in browsing, link clicking. That is a Hermes courier skill; FFS publishes the ingest contract it must satisfy.

**Tasks**: 38 filing cabinet (ADR-028, path families declared in predicate specs), 36 amended, 39 auto-file (ADR-029), 40 courier contract plus `ffs_search` v2 and URL dedup, 41 morning briefing. Build order 38, 36, 40, 39, 41: review by hand until the eval corpus earns auto-file.

ADR-028: "Path families are declared in predicate specs; the business-graph predicate set". Date 2026-09-14. Context: ADR-011 fixed three path families as a hardcoded PathFamily enum (path.rs) with family_for_predicate mapping only three predicates, so adding a predicate does not add a folder; the newspaper / movers-and-shakers goal (read the local business press end to end each morning, keep files on people, orgs, events current) needs four drawers; PRD open question "path library extensibility" said the mechanism is path-definition atoms but UX open. Decision: (1) predicate TOML gains a `[path]` table: `family = "orgs"` (folder root), `name_field = "display_name"` (already implied by pagination.group_field; keep consistent), and the registry becomes the source of truth for families; PathFamily becomes registry-backed (enum replaced or backed by a lookup), path.rs parse/path_for_entity/family_for_predicate take the registry, materializer and plugin enumeration read families from `predicate.inspect`/a new `path.families` RPC rather than a constant list; the three starter specs declare their existing families so behavior is byte-identical for contacts/people/notes. Reject "path-definition atoms" for now (an atom-authored folder is a heavier mechanism than a TOML line, and specs are already git-versioned and hot-reloaded; revisit if users need per-substrate folders without editing specs) and reject "extend the enum by hand" (repeats the bug). (2) Ship four business-graph predicate changes in starter/: `org.company` (display_name required; aliases[], industry, location, website, description, notes[], tags[], history[]), `source.article` (title, url required; publication, byline, published_at, summary, mentions[] of entity ids or names, tags[]), `event.business` (kind enum [funding, acquisition, hire, departure, expansion, opening, closing, award, partnership, other], date, parties[], amount, summary, source url, tags[]), and person.generic bumped to version 2 adding organization, aliases[], mentions[] (dated "YYYY-MM-DD: <what> (<article title>)" strings). Explain why person.generic is extended rather than a new predicate (contacts stay for people you know; person.generic is the movers-and-shakers file; promotion is a later briefing feature). State the copyright/bulk decision: articles store title, url, publication, date, summary, mentions, never full text. (3) Templates emit Obsidian wikilinks: organization renders as [[Org_Display_Name]] using the same slug the entity id uses, article mentions and event parties render as wikilinks, so Obsidian's graph view is the business graph; note the constraint that wikilinks resolve by basename so entity slugs must be unique across families or use family-qualified links (`[[orgs/by-name/A/Acme]]` style) — pick basename-unique slugs with a documented collision rule and say why. Consequences: new stable surface (the `[path]` table joins the TOML predicate-spec format under stability commitments), plugin enumeration changes, materializer writes four new roots. Risks: predicate version bump for person.generic and how the loader treats version (check predicate/mod.rs and say what actually happens). References: ADR-011, ADR-021, ADR-014, ADR-005, ADR-022, ADR-027, task_38, task_36.

ADR-029: "Capability-gated auto-filing of additive proposals". Date 2026-09-14. Context: the goal is a clerk that files the morning's business press into the cabinet without the owner clicking accept on 30+ cards a day, but the quarantine is the AARM Approval Service and the human-in-the-loop fence; batch approval is a listed anti-pattern; the fix must not weaken the fence, it must make the fence policy-as-data. Decision: (1) a new capability Action `Accept` (rename if the codebase's naming suggests better, e.g. `AutoAccept`), granted via an ordinary capability.grant atom to a grantee agent identity (the courier/scribe identity from ffs_author_atom provenance or an ingest source prefix) scoped to predicates and optionally classifications; evaluated by the same evaluator, no new policy code. (2) The additive rule: auto-accept fires only when the proposal is additive: creates a new entity (task_36's `resolution: new`) or appends to additive sections (mentions[], history[], notes[], tags[]) of an existing entity, or creates a new source.article/event.business record. Any proposal that would supersede an existing scalar field (role, organization, title, location) or that the scribe flagged with a parse-warning/low-confidence rationale ALWAYS routes to review. This is AARM Context-Dependent Allow with the context being "additive vs conflicting", and it is exactly the convention's "never silently overwrite" rule (ADR-027) enforced by the substrate. (3) Auto-accepted atoms carry provenance `kind: auto_accept` with the capability atom hash that authorized them (mirrors the federation rule that the receiver records the authorizing capability hash). (4) The daily summary gets an "auto-filed" section: count, the entities touched, and a one-click undo per item that supersedes the auto-accepted atom with a retraction (valid_to now) rather than erasing, so history is kept. (5) Default off: no Accept grant exists on a fresh substrate; the owner grants it explicitly (CLI `ffs capability grant --action accept --grantee <id> --predicates ...`, check ffs-cli commands.rs for the real verb shape and propose a matching one). Alternatives: batch-accept button in the plugin (rejected: it is the anti-pattern, no scoping, no receipt); auto-accept everything from a trusted agent (rejected: role changes overwrite silently); confidence-threshold auto-accept from the LLM engine (deferred: confidence is not calibrated until task_36's corpus scores exist; can be added as a scope condition later). Consequences: capability evaluator gains an action (stable surface, hence this ADR); quarantine needs the additive/conflict classifier, which depends on task_36's `resolution` field and on the predicate spec's additive_sections list (already in the TOML rendering table); risk of an agent flooding the cabinet with new entities (mitigation: the auditor's existing author-rate flag plus a per-grant daily cap in the capability scope, e.g. `max_per_day`). References: ADR-007, ADR-013, ADR-027, ADR-028, ARCHITECTURE.md security model, task_29, task_36, task_39.

Design context you must honor: ADR-028 (being written by another fork) adds registry-declared path families and predicates org.company, source.article (title, url required; publication, byline, published_at, summary, mentions[], tags[]), event.business, and person.generic v2 (organization, aliases[], mentions[]). ADR-029 adds capability-gated auto-filing. task_36 (amended) makes the scribe multi-entity with daemon-side entity resolution. The overall goal: a Hermes agent reads the Charlotte Business Journal email each morning, opens every link with the owner's logged-in session, and files each article into FFS; FFS radiates files to the Obsidian vault; the owner gets an up-to-date local business graph and a morning briefing on movers and shakers. Fetching, logged-in browsing, and link clicking are NOT FFS; FFS publishes the contract the courier must satisfy.

task_40: title "Courier intake contract + `ffs_search` v2 + URL dedup (the newspaper comes in)", complexity medium, dependencies task_36, task_37, task_38. Requirements MUST cover: (1) the ingest contract for an article: a markdown file in `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/` with YAML frontmatter `predicate: source.article`, `title`, `url`, `publication`, `published_at`, `byline`, `tags`, and a body that is the agent-written summary plus a `## Mentions` section of people/orgs (name + one-line role context) and optional `## Events` section; the scribe honors an explicit `predicate:` frontmatter hint (check extraction.py for existing frontmatter handling) and never stores full article text (the contract says the courier must not include it; the scribe truncates bodies over N chars with a parse-warning); (2) URL dedup: a second submission with the same normalized url (scheme/host lowercased, tracking params stripped, trailing slash) resolves to the existing source.article entity (task_36's resolution) so re-reads update rather than duplicate; entity id for articles derived from publication + date + slug of title; (3) the daily digest: the courier drops one `note` per day titled "CBJ digest YYYY-MM-DD" whose References section lists every article filed that day (wikilinks), so "did I read the paper end to end" is answerable; (4) `ffs_search` v2: `entity.search` matches across all string and string-array claim fields declared in the predicate spec (display_name, title, aliases, organization, tags, publication) instead of the hardcoded name field; optional `predicate` filter and `family` filter; hits gain `path` (projection path via path_for_entity) and a `matched_on` field, keeping the lightweight shape; MCP tool schema updated; still capability-filtered; a simple relevance order (exact name match first, then alias, then other fields); (5) an FFS-side reference skill for the courier at `docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md` (instructional, host-agnostic: Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code): the loop (read the email, enumerate links, open each with the user's session, write one ingest file per article per the contract, write the digest note, then call ffs_search to confirm filing or report failures per the convention's persistence honesty), explicit statements that credentials and terms-of-use are the owner's responsibility and that no fetch logic lives in FFS, and a worked example ingest file; (6) docs: docs/agent-memory/README.md lists the courier skill; first-use-guide gets a "read the paper for me" section. Tests: url normalization unit tests (Python, in the scribe or a small `_lib` helper — keep stdlib only), dedup e2e in ingest_pipeline_e2e (same url twice → one entity, two provenance entries), entity.search tests for alias and tag matches and predicate filter, MCP ffs_search tests for the new args, a fixture ingest file that round-trips to a source.article proposal with mentions. Subtasks 40.1–40.7. Success criteria: two hand-dropped CBJ-shaped article files plus a digest note yield articles/, people/, orgs/ files in the vault with wikilinks, and `ffs_search "Acme"` finds the org by alias.

task_41: title "Morning briefing: movers-and-shakers summary from the auditor (what we do next)", complexity medium, dependencies task_13, task_38, task_39, task_40. Requirements MUST cover: (1) a new auditor output `auditor.briefing` atom (weekly by default, daily configurable via env) computed from atoms since the last briefing: people newly seen (new person.generic entities), role/organization changes (superseded scalar fields on people), orgs trending (mention counts over the window vs prior window), events by kind, promotion candidates (person.generic mentioned ≥ N times across ≥ M articles, or mentioned alongside an existing contact's org) → suggest promoting to contact.person, follow-up suggestions (existing contacts whose org appeared in the news), and the auto-filed count from ADR-029; five-items-max panel discipline stays for the daily health summary, the briefing is a separate longer atom; (2) rendered into the vault as `briefings/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (a fifth path family declared per ADR-028, predicate `auditor.briefing` with its own template) so it is readable in Obsidian and in `ffs cat`; (3) plugin: a "Briefing" section or tab in the daily summary panel that renders the latest briefing and offers "promote to contact" (creates a contact.person proposal from the person.generic head, into quarantine, per the human gate) and "dismiss"; (4) MCP: `ffs_audit_query` gains a `kind` filter (`daily_summary` | `briefing`) so an agent can read the briefing and draft outreach; (5) new daemon RPCs only if needed (check whether atom.list by predicate over a tx_time window suffices; prefer no new RPC). Python stdlib only for the auditor per ADR-009. Tests: briefing computation unit tests over fixture atoms (new person, role change, trending org, promotion threshold), template render test, plugin vitest for the section, MCP test for the kind filter, an e2e that files two articles then runs the auditor tick and asserts a briefing atom and a briefings/ file. Subtasks 41.1–41.7. Success criteria: after a week of courier drops, opening Obsidian shows one briefing file that answers "who moved, what's new, who should I call".

content.text:
Committed as `402a3e8` on main, not pushed. The plan now validates at 41 tasks. Here is what I decided, framed as the questions I wish you had asked, and the answers you may want to override.

**What is "reading the paper end-to-end" in FFS terms?** One `source.article` record per article, holding title, url, publication, date, byline, an agent-written summary, and the people and orgs mentioned. Plus one daily digest note listing every article filed, so "did I finish the paper" is a query. Full article text is never stored. The URL is the provenance anchor and the summary is the memory. Override if you want quotes or full text for personal use.

**What are the filing cabinets?** Four drawers: `people/` for movers and shakers (person.generic extended with organization, aliases, dated mentions), `orgs/`, `events/` (funding, acquisition, hire, departure, expansion, opening, closing, award, partnership), and `articles/`. `contacts/` stays for people you actually know. Promotion from people to contacts is a briefing suggestion, never automatic.

**How do drawers become a graph?** Templates emit wikilinks, so a person's org, an article's mentions, and an event's parties all resolve in Obsidian's graph view. This needs path families to become data declared in predicate TOML instead of the hardcoded three-variant enum. That is ADR-028 and task_38, and it is why task_38 goes first.

**Does the clerk file automatically?** Yes, but only additive things. ADR-029 adds an `Accept` capability you grant to the courier's identity, scoped to predicates with a daily cap. New entities, new articles, new events, and appended history file themselves. Anything that would overwrite an existing fact, such as a role change, always lands in your review. The daily summary shows what was auto-filed with an undo. Default is off, so you review by hand until the scribe's eval corpus earns your trust.

**How does the same person across fifty articles stay one file?** Task_36 gains daemon-side entity resolution by name and alias, tagging each proposal `existing` or `new`. Task_40 adds URL dedup and upgrades `ffs_search` to match aliases, orgs, and tags. Aliases you add by hand ("Bob Smith" is "Robert Smith") are the escape hatch. Fuzzy matching is out of scope.

**What do we do next, regularly?** Task_41: a weekly briefing atom rendered to `briefings/` in the vault. It lists new people, role and org changes, trending orgs, events by kind, people seen often enough to promote, and contacts whose org made the news. "Promote to contact" is one click that creates a quarantined proposal.

**What is not FFS?** The email, the logged-in browser, the link clicking. Task_40 publishes the ingest contract and a reference courier skill for Hermes, with credentials and terms of use stated as your responsibility.

**Build order and effort**

| Task | What | Size |
|---|---|---|
| 38 | Filing cabinet, ADR-028 | high |
| 36 | Scribe v2, amended | high |
| 40 | Courier contract, search v2, dedup | medium |
| 39 | Auto-file, ADR-029 | high |
| 41 | Morning briefing | medium |

Two things the forks noticed that are worth knowing: the daemon has no periodic auditor driver wired today, so task_41 adds one, and the scribe never fills a note's references list, which task_40 takes on because the digest depends on it.

When you're ready, I'll start task_38.

input.description: Research: entity resolution, Wikipedia/Wikidata
input.prompt:
Research track 1. Question: "How does the same person across fifty articles stay one file?" Find how Wikipedia/Wikidata does this when it does it best, plus the academic and industry best practice for entity resolution / entity linking / record linkage, and write a sourced research memo at docs/research/2026-09-14-entity-resolution.md. Do not edit any other file. Do not commit. Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them with ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" in one call). Verify claims against fetched sources; cite URLs; mark anything you could not verify as unverified. No em-dashes in the memo.

Cover at least, verifying each against a real source:
1. Wikipedia's identity mechanics: one article per topic, redirects (including redirect-on-merge and how page history merges work), disambiguation pages and hatnotes, naming conventions for people with identical names (parenthetical disambiguators), the "notability" gate as a NIL policy, and the fact that the article title is NOT the identity: Wikidata's QID is (Q-items are stable, opaque, never reused; merged items become redirects; "said to be the same as" P460 vs "different from" P1889; aliases as first-class; labels per language; sitelinks). Look at Wikidata's Help:Merge and Help:Aliases and the property pages for P1889/P460.
2. Academic entity linking / wikification lineage: Bunescu & Pasca 2006, Mihalcea & Csomai 2007 (Wikify), Cucerzan 2007, Milne & Witten 2008, TAC-KBP entity linking and NIL clustering (Ji & Grishman), AIDA (Hoffart 2011), and neural era BLINK (Wu et al. 2020, bi-encoder candidate retrieval + cross-encoder rerank), GENRE (De Cao 2021, autoregressive entity names), and the standard pipeline: mention detection, candidate generation (alias tables, prior probability p(entity|mention)), disambiguation using context and coherence, NIL detection and NIL clustering. Report typical accuracy numbers with sources.
3. Record linkage / entity resolution lineage: Fellegi and Sunter 1969 decision model, Christen's Data Matching (blocking, comparison, classification, evaluation), Getoor and Machanavajjhala's ER tutorial (collective ER), Dedupe/Splink style probabilistic linkage, the merge/split problem and why systems keep "cluster ids" separate from record ids.
4. Industry identifier practice: W3C Reconciliation Service API (OpenRefine) shape (query, candidates with scores and match flag), MusicBrainz MBID merge-redirect behavior, ORCID for people, the Google Knowledge Graph MID redirect history if verifiable, Wikidata's redirect handling in SPARQL (owl:sameAs). Also Obsidian's own aliases frontmatter and how wikilinks resolve to aliases (verify in Obsidian docs).
5. Human-in-the-loop practice: how Wikidata handles wrong merges (undo via redirect reversal, "different from" to prevent re-merge), and any research on active learning / reviewer effort in ER (e.g., Dedupe's active labeling).

Then a final section "Design implications for FFS" that maps findings onto FFS's actual mechanics (you know them: atoms about an entity id, supersession chains, bitemporal validity, provenance, quarantine review, aliases[] planned in person.generic v2, task_36's daemon-side resolution with resolution: existing|new, ADR-029's additive/conflict rule, wikilinks resolving by basename). Recommend concretely: opaque stable entity ids vs slug ids (what Wikidata teaches; how to keep human-readable projections if ids are opaque); an alias table and prior probability from the substrate's own history; candidate generation + disambiguation using article context (organization, location, role) and coherence with other mentions in the same article; a NIL policy (when to mint a new entity vs route to review); a merge mechanism as a signed "entity.same_as" or redirect atom so merges are reversible and history is kept; a "entity.different_from" assertion as the human-override that prevents re-merge; confidence thresholds with three outcomes (auto-link, auto-new, review) and how ADR-029 should consume them; evaluation via the golden corpus (pairwise precision/recall, B-cubed). Be specific about which of these are Phase 1 (task_36/38/40) and which are later. About 300 to 400 lines. Report the file path and the five most important findings in one line each.

input.description: Research: ISO 21838, BFO, TUpper
input.prompt:
Research track 2. Study ISO/IEC 21838 (Top-level ontologies: Part 1 requirements, Part 2 Basic Formal Ontology, Part 3 DOLCE, Part 4 TUpper), Basic Formal Ontology (BFO 2020), and TUpper (the Toronto upper ontology, Michael Grüninger and colleagues, Common Logic based), and write a sourced research memo at docs/research/2026-09-14-top-level-ontologies.md. Do not edit any other file. Do not commit. Use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them with ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" in one call). Verify claims against fetched sources (ISO catalogue pages, the BFO GitHub repo and documentation, basic-formal-ontology.org, the TUpper papers or the ISO 21838-4 page, Grüninger's publications, the IAO Information Artifact Ontology for "information content entity" and "is about"); cite URLs; mark anything unverified. No em-dashes.

Cover:
1. ISO/IEC 21838-1: what a top-level ontology must provide (the requirements: axiomatization in OWL 2 and Common Logic, documentation, bridging, etc.), and what conformance means for a domain ontology. Publication years and current status of each part.
2. BFO 2020 core: continuant vs occurrent; independent continuant (material entity, object such as a person or an organization as a group of persons? check how BFO treats organizations, often via an extension), specifically dependent continuant (quality, role, disposition, function), generically dependent continuant (information content entity via IAO), process, process boundary, temporal region, spatial region, site; the relations: participates in, bearer of, realizes, concretizes, is about (IAO), part of, located in, occupies temporal region. Role in BFO: a realizable entity borne by a continuant, exists because of social circumstances, realized in processes. Explain exactly how "Jane Doe is CEO of Acme from 2024" is modeled in BFO: person (object) bearer of a CEO role; the role inheres in the person; the role exists during a temporal region; it is realized in processes (running the company); organization as an object aggregate or as a social entity in common extensions (CCO Common Core Ontologies: Organization, Agent, Affiliation? verify what CCO provides). Cite the BFO 2020 documentation and CCO if used.
3. TUpper: what it is (a top-level ontology from the University of Toronto assembled from PSL, mereotopology, time, etc.), how it is axiomatized (Common Logic modules, the COLORE repository), how it differs from BFO (process-centric, first-order, activity occurrences, fluents/state), and its ISO 21838-4 status. Verify with primary sources.
4. DOLCE briefly for contrast (endurant/perdurant, qualities, descriptions and situations), only as much as needed to explain why one would pick BFO vs TUpper vs DOLCE for a personal records substrate.
5. IAO: information content entity, "is about", document, and how a news article about a person is modeled (article is a generically dependent continuant concretized in a file; it is about the person; it has a creation date and author).

Then a final section "Design implications for FFS" that maps the ontology onto FFS's actual predicate design (you know it: atoms about an entity with a predicate and a JSON claim, bitemporal valid_from/valid_to, supersession chains, provenance; planned predicates contact.person, person.generic v2 with organization/aliases/mentions, org.company, source.article with mentions, event.business with kind/parties/date; capability atoms). Answer concretely: (a) should "organization" be a field on the person (current ADR-028 plan) or should an affiliation/role be its own atom, as BFO's role-as-dependent-continuant suggests, with the person as bearer, the org as the context, valid_from/valid_to as the role's temporal region, and supersession when the role ends? Give the tradeoffs for FFS (projection rendering, wikilinks, fast-path edits, the additive/conflict rule in ADR-029, queries like "who was CEO of Acme in 2024") and recommend one; (b) is event.business an occurrent with participants, and does that imply a `participants` structure (entity id + role-in-event) rather than a flat parties[] of names; (c) is source.article an IAO information content entity, and should "mentions" be "is about" links to entity ids rather than names; (d) whether FFS should declare BFO alignment in predicate specs (e.g., a `bfo_class` or `iso21838` annotation in the TOML) and what that buys (interoperability, federation vocabulary agreement between peers, future OWL export) versus the cost; (e) what NOT to adopt (full OWL reasoning, rigid class hierarchies) and why, for a personal substrate. Mark what should change in ADR-028 / task_38 / task_36 vs what is later. About 300 to 400 lines. Report the file path and the five most important findings in one line each.

130:### 6.2 The alias table and priors come from the substrate's own history (Phase 1, task_36 + task_40)

168:### 6.6 NIL policy: when to mint (Phase 1, task_36; refined in task_41)
176:### 6.7 Evaluation (Phase 1, task_36's corpus)

186:## 7. Phase summary
205:## 8. Sources fetched or searched in this session
=====
## 6. Design implications for FFS

FFS already has most of the pieces: atoms about an entity id, supersession chains that preserve history, bitemporal validity, provenance on every claim, a quarantine that is the human gate, `aliases[]` planned on `person.generic` v2 (ADR-028), daemon-side resolution with `resolution: existing | new` (task_36 as amended), the additive-versus-conflict rule (ADR-029), and wikilinks that resolve by file basename. What follows maps the findings onto those pieces and says which task owns each.

### 6.1 Identity: opaque entity ids, names as data (Phase 1, task_38 + task_36)

Wikidata's lesson is that the identifier must be meaningless and permanent, and the human-readable name must be data that can change. Today an FFS entity id is a slug derived from the display name (task_32), which is Wikipedia's *title*, not Wikidata's *QID*. That works until the first rename, merge, or two people with the same name.

Recommendation:

- Mint entity ids as opaque, stable strings (a short random id or a hash of the first proposal's content plus a nonce; the exact form is a task_38 decision) for every new entity created by the scribe or the MCP path. Never derive them from the name.
- Keep the projection *file name* human-readable: `people/by-name/S/Sara_Chen.md`. The materializer maps entity id to path through `path_for_entity` using the head atom's `display_name`; the mapping is a projection concern, not an identity concern. A rename supersedes `display_name`, the materializer moves the file, and the old basename is left as a one-line redirect note ("Moved to [[Sara_Chen-Acme]]") so existing wikilinks keep resolving, which is exactly Wikipedia's redirect-on-move.
- Collisions get Wikipedia's parenthetical, applied to the *file name only*: `Sara_Chen_(Acme).md` and `Sara_Chen_(City_Council).md`, with the qualifier taken from `organization` first, then `role`, then a year. ADR-028's "family token suffix" rule should be replaced by this, because a qualifier a human recognizes beats a token nobody does.
- Put `aliases` into every projection's frontmatter so Obsidian's link completion and search find the file by any name, and emit links as `[[Sara_Chen_(Acme)|Sara Chen]]` so the display text can be the natural name while the target is the unique basename.

### 6.2 The alias table and priors come from the substrate's own history (Phase 1, task_36 + task_40)

Wikidata maintains aliases by hand; Milne and Witten got priors from anchor text. FFS has both for free:

- **Aliases**: `display_name`, `aliases[]`, and every surface form that has ever been resolved to this entity by an accepted proposal. When the owner accepts a proposal whose mention text was "S. Chen" and whose resolved entity is Sara Chen, append "S. Chen" to her aliases (an additive edit, so ADR-029 can auto-file it).
- **Prior**: for a surface form that maps to several entities, p(entity given form) is the count of accepted resolutions to each, from the atom store. This is "commonness". A new substrate has no counts; fall back to "most recently mentioned" and then to review.
- **`entity.search` v2** (task_40) is the candidate generator. Its `matched_on` field should distinguish `display_name`, `alias`, and `other`, and its ordering should be exact name, then alias, then prior count. This is also the W3C reconciliation shape; consider exposing it as such over MCP later so any reconciliation-aware tool (OpenRefine included) can talk to a substrate.

### 6.3 Disambiguation uses article context and coherence (Phase 1 minimal, later full)

- **Blocking**: candidates come only from the same family (people vs orgs) and from a normalized surname or organization-name key. Nothing else is compared.
- **Context features** (Phase 1, task_36's daemon-side resolver): agreement between the candidate's head atoms and the proposal's fields for `organization`, `role`, `location`. Fellegi-Sunter weights, hand-set to start: organization agreement is strong evidence (high m, low u), a shared surname alone is weak (high u for common names). Store the weights in a TOML next to the predicate specs so they are tunable without code.
- **Coherence** (later): if the same article also proposes an org that the candidate person is already affiliated with, raise that candidate.
