# Task 38: Filing cabinet — registry-declared path families + business-graph predicates and wikilinked templates (ADR-028, amended by ADR-030/031)

## Overview
The morning-briefing goal (read the local business press end to end, keep files on the movers and shakers current) needs four drawers: people, organizations, articles, events. The substrate has three, and they are hardcoded: `PathFamily` in `crates/ffs-core/src/projection/path.rs` is a closed enum, `family_for_predicate` maps exactly three predicate names, the materializer silently drops any atom outside them, `dispatch.rs::entity_search` special-cases `"note" => "title"`, and the Obsidian plugin carries its own `PROJECTION_FAMILIES` constant. Registering a predicate today gives you a schema and a template but no folder. ADR-028 decides that the predicate spec declares its own family via a `[path]` table, that the registry becomes the source of truth every consumer reads, that the business-graph predicate set ships in `starter/`, and that templates emit Obsidian wikilinks so the vault's graph view is the business graph. This task implements all of it with the three-family byte-identity check as the gate before any new spec lands.

Amended 2026-09-14 (ADR-030, ADR-031). Two research tracks on "how does the same person across fifty articles stay one file" changed the shapes before implementation started. Entity ids become opaque and permanent (ADR-030); the human-readable name is data on the head atom, the file name is a projection concern, collisions get a parenthetical qualifier on the file name, and renames or merges leave a redirect stub. Roles become their own `affiliation` atoms rendered into person and org files by reverse lookup; event participants and article mentions become entity references, not strings; predicate specs may carry an informative `[ontology]` table (ADR-031). Two identity predicates, `entity.same_as` and `entity.different_from`, join the starter set, and a starter `config/resolution.toml` carries the weights and thresholds task_36's resolver consumes. The family-token collision suffix from the original ADR-028 text is withdrawn.

Ordered after task_36 on purpose (2026-09-14): the tracer bullet's real extraction output informs the spec shapes and the resolver config; the resolver itself is task_45.

<critical>
- ALWAYS READ the PRD and TechSpec before starting
- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here
- FOCUS ON "WHAT" — describe what needs to be accomplished, not how
- MINIMIZE CODE — show code only to illustrate current structure or problem areas
- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

<requirements>
- MUST add an optional `[path]` table (`family`, `name_field`) and an optional `[ontology]` table (`bfo`, `cco`, `iao`, `note`, all strings) to the predicate-spec loader (`RawSpec` and `PredicateSpec` in `crates/ffs-core/src/predicate/mod.rs`; the loader is `deny_unknown_fields`, so both tables have to be declared there). A spec whose `path.name_field` disagrees with `pagination.group_field` MUST fail to load with a clear error. Specs without `[path]` MUST still load and have no projection family. `[ontology]` MUST be informative only: unknown or empty values MUST NOT fail the load, and nothing in the daemon MUST branch on it.
- MUST make path families registry-backed: `PathFamily::try_parse`, `primary_predicate`, `as_str`, `family_for_predicate`, and `path_for_entity` in `path.rs` resolve through the registry (or a family table snapshot derived from it) instead of a closed enum. The renderer (`projection/render.rs`), materializer (`ffs-daemon/src/materializer.rs`), fast-path watcher (`ffs-fastpath/src/watcher.rs`), and `entity_search` (`ffs-daemon/src/dispatch.rs`, which MUST derive the name field from the spec's `path.name_field` and drop the hardcoded `"note"` match) MUST all consume the registry-backed family.
- MUST keep behavior byte-identical for `contacts/`, `people/`, `notes/`: the three starter specs gain `[path]` tables declaring their existing families, every existing test in `path.rs`, `render.rs`, `materializer.rs`, and the fastpath crate passes with assertions unmodified, and materialized output for the existing fixtures is unchanged except for the new `aliases:` frontmatter line, which MUST be suppressed when the claim has no aliases so existing fixtures stay byte-identical.
- MUST add a `path.families` JSON-RPC method to the daemon returning `[{family, predicate, name_field}]` for every spec that declares `[path]`, and MUST make the Obsidian plugin enumerate families from it (`paths.ts` `PROJECTION_FAMILIES` and `main.ts` `familyForPredicate` replaced by a runtime table; `folder.ts` enumeration and `isProjectionPath` consult it). The plugin MUST tolerate the daemon being unreachable at load (empty or last-known table, no crash).
- MUST mint opaque entity ids per ADR-030: a helper in `ffs-core` (`EntityId::mint()`: 16 random bytes, base58btc multibase, `z` prefix) replaces `slug_for_proposal` as the id source in `dispatch.rs::ingest_accept` for every new entity. Existing slug-form ids MUST remain valid (they are just strings; nothing may assume the new form). The `from-<submission-id>` fallback MUST be deleted.
- MUST move the human-readable name to the projection layer: the materializer and working set MUST keep a persisted path-to-entity index (`working_set.rs` plus the SQLite working-set table) so that `path_for_entity` derives the basename from the head atom's name field, a rename supersedes the name and moves the file, and the old basename is left as a one-line redirect stub (`Moved to [[<new basename>|<display>]]`) that the fast-path watcher ignores. `parse` of a projection path MUST resolve the basename through the index to the entity id.
- MUST apply ADR-030's collision rule on the file name only: when two entities in any family would share a basename, the second and later get a parenthetical qualifier taken from `organization`, then `role`, then the year of `valid_from` (`Sara_Chen_(Acme).md`, `Sara_Chen_(City_Council).md`). The rule lives in one place (the path-to-entity index) and MUST be deterministic for a given set of head atoms. The family-token suffix rule from the original ADR-028 text MUST NOT be implemented.
- MUST ship the starter spec changes, each with `claim_schema`, `[rendering]`, `[[reverse_map]]` rules, `[pagination]` (where the family has listings), `[path]` (where the predicate has a folder), and `[ontology]`:
  - new `org.company.toml` (family `orgs`; `display_name` required, `aliases[]`, `industry`, `location`, `website`, `description`, `notes[]`, `tags[]`, `history[]`);
  - new `source.article.toml` (family `articles`, pagination `recency`; `title` and `url` required, `publication`, `byline`, `published_at`, `summary`, `content_hash`, `mentions[]` of `{entity, display, context}` objects with `display` required, `tags[]`);
  - new `event.business.toml` (family `events`, pagination `recency`; `kind` enum per ADR-028, `date`, `participants[]` of `{entity, display, role}` objects with `display` required and `role` from ADR-031's enum, `amount`, `summary`, `source`, `tags[]`);
  - new `affiliation.toml` (no `[path]`; `person` and `organization` entity ids required, `title`, `kind` enum per ADR-031, `source`, `notes[]`);

## Implementation Details
Current structure: `PathFamily` (closed enum, `path.rs`) → `ParsedPath` → `render.rs` (`primary_predicate()` picks the store query; the Tera context is `entity`, `claim`, `classification`) and `materializer.rs` (`family_for_predicate` → `path_for_entity`). The plugin mirrors the enum in `paths.ts` and `main.ts`. The spec loader (`predicate/mod.rs`) already parses `[pagination] group_field`; the `[path]` and `[ontology]` tables sit beside it. Entity ids today are `slug_for_proposal` in `dispatch.rs` (task_32), which is the Wikipedia-title anti-pattern ADR-030 retires.

Shape sketch for the registry-backed family and the reverse lookup (illustrative only):

```rust
pub struct PathFamily { folder: String, predicate: PredicateName, name_field: String }
// resolved via registry.family_for_folder("orgs") / registry.family_for_predicate(&pred)

// render_single_entity, after the head atom and capability check:
let affiliations = store.list_by_predicate(&PredicateName::new("affiliation"), None, 1000)?
    .into_iter().filter(|a| a.claim["person"] == entity.as_str())  // or ["organization"] for orgs
    /* head-of-chain and as_of filtering */;
ctx.insert("affiliations", &affiliations);
```

Version bump: the loader stores `version` and nothing reads it (no migration hook; `validate_claim` keys on name). Additive changes are safe; the starter README documents that a breaking change needs a new predicate name until a migration mechanism exists.

Redirect stubs: a stub is a projection file whose whole body is one line; the materializer records its hash in the suppression registry like any other write, and the watcher treats a file matching the stub shape as not-an-edit. Stubs are never atoms.

## Overview
The morning-briefing goal (read the local business press end to end, keep files on the movers and shakers current) needs four drawers: people, organizations, articles, events. The substrate has three, and they are hardcoded: `PathFamily` in `crates/ffs-core/src/projection/path.rs` is a closed enum, `family_for_predicate` maps exactly three predicate names, the materializer silently drops any atom outside them, `dispatch.rs::entity_search` special-cases `"note" => "title"`, and the Obsidian plugin carries its own `PROJECTION_FAMILIES` constant. Registering a predicate today gives you a schema and a template but no folder. ADR-028 decides that the predicate spec declares its own family via a `[path]` table, that the registry becomes the source of truth every consumer reads, that the business-graph predicate set ships in `starter/`, and that templates emit Obsidian wikilinks so the vault's graph view is the business graph. This task implements all of it with the three-family byte-identity check as the gate before any new spec lands.

Amended 2026-09-14 (ADR-030, ADR-031). Two research tracks on "how does the same person across fifty articles stay one file" changed the shapes before implementation started. Roles become their own `affiliation` atoms rendered into person and org files by reverse lookup; event participants and article mentions become entity references, not strings; predicate specs may carry an informative `[ontology]` table (ADR-031). Two identity predicates, `entity.same_as` and `entity.different_from`, join the starter set, and a starter `config/resolution.toml` carries the weights and thresholds task_36's resolver consumes. ## Implementation Details
Current structure: `PathFamily` (closed enum, `path.rs`) → `ParsedPath` → `render.rs` (`primary_predicate()` picks the store query; the Tera context is `entity`, `claim`, `classification`) and `materializer.rs` (`family_for_predicate` → `path_for_entity`). The plugin mirrors the enum in `paths.ts` and `main.ts`. The spec loader (`predicate/mod.rs`) already parses `[pagination] group_field`; the `[path]` and `[ontology]` tables sit beside it. Entity ids today are `slug_for_proposal` in `dispatch.rs` (task_32), which is the Wikipedia-title anti-pattern ADR-030 retires.

Shape sketch for the registry-backed family and the reverse lookup (illustrative only):

```rust
pub struct PathFamily { folder: String, predicate: PredicateName, name_field: String }
// resolved via registry.family_for_folder("orgs") / registry.family_for_predicate(&pred)

// render_single_entity, after the head atom and capability check:
let affiliations = store.list_by_predicate(&PredicateName::new("affiliation"), None, 1000)?
    .into_iter().filter(|a| a.claim["person"] == entity.as_str())  // or ["organization"] for orgs
    /* head-of-chain and as_of filtering */;
ctx.insert("affiliations", &affiliations);
```

Version bump: the loader stores `version` and nothing reads it (no migration hook; `validate_claim` keys on name). Additive changes are safe; the starter README documents that a breaking change needs a new predicate name until a migration mechanism exists.

Redirect stubs: a stub is a projection file whose whole body is one line; the materializer records its hash in the suppression registry like any other write, and the watcher treats a file matching the stub shape as not-an-edit. Stubs are never atoms.

Run `npm test` in obsidian-plugin/ and report the summary, the exported API of paths.ts, and any assumption you made about the RPC shape.

input.prompt:
You own the starter specs, templates, and docs half of task_38 (read .compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/task_38.md fully, adr-028, adr-030, adr-031, starter/predicates/README.md, starter/templates/README.md, the three existing specs and templates, and docs/research/2026-09-14-top-level-ontologies.md section 6 for the ontology rows). Files you own: starter/predicates/*.toml (new org.company, source.article, event.business, affiliation, entity.same_as, entity.different_from; person.generic bumped to version 2; contact.person may gain [ontology] tweaks only), starter/templates/*.tera (new org-company, source-article, event-business; updated person-generic and contact-person), starter/predicates/README.md, starter/templates/README.md, docs/ontology-alignment.md (new), ARCHITECTURE.md (path-library prose, stability line naming [path], entity-id prose), crates/ffs-mcp/src/tools.rs (ffs_list_path description examples only), installer/install.sh and install.ps1 (copy starter/config/resolution.toml to $FFS_DATA_DIR/config/). Do NOT touch crates/ffs-core, crates/ffs-daemon, crates/ffs-fastpath, obsidian-plugin (other forks). Do not commit. No em-dashes in prose.

Already on disk: the three starter specs carry `[path]` and `[ontology]` tables (contacts/display_name, people/display_name, notes/title); the loader accepts `[path] {family, name_field}` (name_field must equal pagination.group_field when both exist) and `[ontology] {bfo, cco, iao, note}` (all free strings); `starter/config/resolution.toml` exists.

Template context the renderer will provide (another fork is implementing it; code against exactly this): `entity`, `claim`, `classification` as today; `organization_link` = `{basename, display}` or null when `claim.organization` does not resolve; `mentions_resolved` = array of `{entity, display, context, basename}` (basename null when unresolved); `participants_resolved` = array of `{entity, display, role, basename}`; `affiliations` = array of `{entity, display, basename, title, kind, valid_from, valid_to, side}` where side is "person" when the rendered entity is the org (so the other party is a person) and "organization" when the rendered entity is a person. Link form: `[[{{ x.basename }}|{{ x.display }}]]` when basename is set, else plain `{{ x.display }}`. Every template emits `aliases:` in frontmatter ONLY when `claim.aliases` is a non-empty array (byte-identity for existing fixtures); the `## Affiliations` (people, contacts) and `## People` (orgs) sections are emitted only when `affiliations` is non-empty, each line `- [[basename|display]]: title (valid_from to valid_to-or-present)` with plain display when basename is null. Keep the determinism and empty-section rules from starter/templates/README.md.

Specs to write, each with claim_schema, [rendering] (frontmatter_fields, body_sections, additive_sections), [[reverse_map]] rules for every rendered field/section, [pagination] where listed, [path] where the predicate has a folder, and [ontology]:
- org.company.toml: family orgs, pagination alphabetical_first_letter/display_name; display_name required; aliases[], industry, location, website, description, notes[], tags[], history[]; additive sections Notes, Tags, History; template org-company.md.tera with a `## People` reverse-lookup section (no reverse_map rule for People; document that edits there route to ingest).
- source.article.toml: family articles, pagination recency, name_field title; title and url required; publication, byline, published_at, summary, content_hash, mentions[] of objects {entity, display (required), context}, tags[]; template source-article.md.tera rendering a `## Mentions` list with links and a `## Summary` body; additive sections Tags (and Mentions only if the reverse-map edit_kind can express an object item; if not, leave Mentions non-additive and say so in the README).
- event.business.toml: family events, pagination recency, name_field summary? No: name_field must be a string field that names the event; use `title` (add `title` required, a short headline) so basenames are readable; kind enum [funding, acquisition, hire, departure, expansion, opening, closing, award, partnership, other] required; date, participants[] of {entity, display (required), role enum [acquirer, target, investor, investee, hire, employer, departing, landlord, tenant, developer, winner, partner, other]}, amount, summary, source, tags[]; template event-business.md.tera with `## Participants` links.
- affiliation.toml: no [path]; person and organization required (entity ids), title, kind enum [employee, executive, board, founder, investor, advisor, member, other], source, notes[]; rendering template affiliation.md.tera minimal (it renders inside person and org files; a standalone template still needed by the loader: keep it tiny).
- entity.same_as.toml: no [path]; target required, reason, criterion; entity.different_from.toml: no [path]; other required, criterion; minimal templates.
- person.generic.toml: version = 2; add organization (string; document: current primary affiliation, rendering convenience only), aliases[], mentions[] (strings "YYYY-MM-DD: what (article title)"); reverse_map rules for each; rendering frontmatter adds organization; body sections add Mentions (additive); template person-generic.md.tera: organization rendered as a link via organization_link, `## Mentions`, `## Affiliations`.
- contact-person.md.tera: add the `## Affiliations` section and `aliases:` line; contact.person.toml may add aliases[] with a reverse-map rule if you also add it to the template (optional; keep byte-identity for fixtures without aliases).
Every [ontology] table must match the row you write in docs/ontology-alignment.md.

docs/ontology-alignment.md: the [ontology] vocabulary (bfo values: continuant, occurrent, object, object aggregate, role, quality, process, information content entity; cco and iao are free identifiers), one row per starter predicate (contact.person and person.generic object; org.company object aggregate; affiliation role; event.business process; source.article and note information content entity; capability.grant, entity.same_as, entity.different_from information content entity; auditor.* information content entity if a spec exists), what alignment buys (design discipline, federation vocabulary agreement, RDF export later), and what is deliberately not adopted, citing ADR-031. starter/predicates/README.md: the [path] and [ontology] tables, the new and updated specs with their reverse-map tables, object shapes for mentions and participants, the version-bump rule (additive keeps the name; breaking needs a new predicate name until a migration mechanism exists), resolution.toml. starter/templates/README.md: link form, aliases line, reverse-lookup sections, the redirect stub shape `Moved to [[new|display]]` and the merged stub `Merged into [[target|display]]`. ARCHITECTURE.md: "Three folder spaces" prose becomes registry-declared families (list the starter set); the stability line for the TOML predicate-spec format names the [path] table; the atom-envelope section notes entity ids are opaque and names are claim data (ADR-030). ffs_list_path description in crates/ffs-mcp/src/tools.rs: add orgs/, articles/, events/ examples (text only). Installer: copy resolution.toml.

Validate what you can without the renderer: `cargo nextest run -p ffs-core predicate` must stay green with your specs loadable (write a test-free check by running the existing registry load test against starter/predicates if one exists; else run `cargo nextest run -p ffs-core` and confirm no spec-loading test broke), and `cargo nextest run -p ffs-mcp` for the description change. Report the file list, the exact reverse-map rule counts per spec, and the template context fields you relied on.

6. `crates/ffs-daemon/tests/ingest_pipeline_e2e.rs`: add an org-note fixture (frontmatter `predicate: org.company`, display_name, industry) dropped, extracted (the scribe's hint path yields... note: the heuristic scribe cannot produce org.company claims; use the dispatcher's `ingest.submit` + a stub scribe in the test that returns an `org.company` proposal, as other daemon tests do) and accepted, asserting the file lands under `orgs/by-name/<L>/` and the entity id is opaque. Keep the existing e2e tests green.
7. `main.rs`: document `config/resolution.toml` presence (loaded at boot via `ResolutionConfig::load`, warn if missing, nothing consumes it yet).

Verify: `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. Also run the byte-identity gate: `cargo nextest run -p ffs-core starter_templates` and the daemon materializer tests, confirming existing expected outputs are unchanged. Report the summary lines, the exact RPC name and hit field added, and anything you had to change in ffs-core/src (should be nothing).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# task_38 subtask 38.11 live check on a SCRATCH substrate (never ~/.ffs/atoms.db):
# drop an org note and a person note naming that org, accept both, confirm files and the wikilink.
set -uo pipefail
REPO="$HOME/Entire/ffs"; HERE="$HOME/.ffs/spikes/task38-live"; SCRATCH="$HERE/scratch"
RPC="$HOME/.ffs/spikes/task36-live/rpc.py"; DAEMON="$REPO/target/debug/ffs-daemon"
pkill -f "$DAEMON" || true; sleep 1
rm -rf "$SCRATCH"; mkdir -p "$SCRATCH"/{config/predicates,config/templates,skills,ingest,run,log}
cp "$REPO"/starter/predicates/*.toml "$SCRATCH/config/predicates/"; cp "$REPO"/starter/templates/*.tera "$SCRATCH/config/templates/"
cp "$REPO"/starter/config/resolution.toml "$SCRATCH/config/"
cp -R "$REPO"/skills/. "$SCRATCH/skills/"; rm -rf "$SCRATCH"/skills/*/__pycache__ "$SCRATCH"/skills/*/tests; chmod 700 "$SCRATCH/run"
export FFS_DATA_DIR="$SCRATCH" FFS_KEYRING_DISABLE=1 FFS_INGEST_STABILITY_MS=2000 FFS_LOG=info
export FFS_OWNER_KEY_HEX=4444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444444
export FFS_SQLCIPHER_KEY_HEX=5555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555
nohup "$DAEMON" > "$SCRATCH/log/daemon.log" 2>&1 &
sleep 4
cat > "$SCRATCH/ingest/Acme Widgets.md" <<'MD'
---
predicate: org.company
display_name: Acme Widgets
industry: manufacturing
location: Gastonia, NC
---
Family-owned widget maker; synthetic validation record.
MD
sleep 8
python3 "$RPC" "$SCRATCH/run/ffs.sock" ingest.list_pending > "$HERE/pending1.json"
python3 - "$HERE/pending1.json" "$SCRATCH/run/ffs.sock" "$RPC" <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, sys
subs = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
for s in subs:
    print("pending:", s["source_uri"].split("/")[-1], [(p["predicate"], p["claim"].get("display_name") or p["claim"].get("title")) for p in s["proposals"]])
    out = subprocess.run(["python3", sys.argv[3], sys.argv[2], "ingest.accept", json.dumps({"submission_id": s["id"]})], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print("accept ->", out.stdout.strip()[:300])
PY
sleep 2
echo "--- files under orgs/:"; find "$SCRATCH/orgs" -type f 2>/dev/null
ORG_FILE=$(find "$SCRATCH/orgs" -type f -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$ORG_FILE" ] && { echo "--- $ORG_FILE:"; cat "$ORG_FILE"; }
# entity id of the org: from entity.search
python3 "$RPC" "$SCRATCH/run/ffs.sock" entity.search '{"query":"acme","limit":5}' > "$HERE/search.json"; cat "$HERE/search.json"
ORG_ID=$(python3 -c "import json;r=json.load(open('$HERE/search.json'));print(r['results'][0]['entity'] if r.get('results') else '')")
echo "org entity id: $ORG_ID"
cat > "$SCRATCH/ingest/Pat Example.md" <<MD
---
predicate: person.generic
display_name: Pat Example
role: CEO
organization: $ORG_ID
---
Runs Acme Widgets; synthetic validation record.
MD
sleep 8
python3 "$RPC" "$SCRATCH/run/ffs.sock" ingest.list_pending > "$HERE/pending2.json"
python3 - "$HERE/pending2.json" "$SCRATCH/run/ffs.sock" "$RPC" <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, sys
for s in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])):
    print("pending:", s["source_uri"].split("/")[-1], [(p["predicate"], p["claim"].get("display_name")) for p in s["proposals"]])
    out = subprocess.run(["python3", sys.argv[3], sys.argv[2], "ingest.accept", json.dumps({"submission_id": s["id"]})], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print("accept ->", out.stdout.strip()[:200])
PY
sleep 2
echo "--- files under people/:"; find "$SCRATCH/people" -type f 2>/dev/null
P_FILE=$(find "$SCRATCH/people" -type f -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$P_FILE" ] && { echo "--- $P_FILE:"; cat "$P_FILE"; }
echo "--- path.families:"; python3 "$RPC" "$SCRATCH/run/ffs.sock" path.families
echo "--- daemon warns:"; sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$SCRATCH/log/daemon.log" | grep -i "warn\|error" | cut -c1-200 | tail -5
EOF
chmod +x ~/.ffs/spikes/task38-live/run.sh; echo "live-check script ready"

14	# Task 38: Filing cabinet — registry-declared path families + business-graph predicates and wikilinked templates (ADR-028, amended by ADR-030/031)
15	
16	## Overview
17	The morning-briefing goal (read the local business press end to end, keep files on the movers and shakers current) needs four drawers: people, organizations, articles, events. The substrate has three, and they are hardcoded: `PathFamily` in `crates/ffs-core/src/projection/path.rs` is a closed enum, `family_for_predicate` maps exactly three predicate names, the materializer silently drops any atom outside them, `dispatch.rs::entity_search` special-cases `"note" => "title"`, and the Obsidian plugin carries its own `PROJECTION_FAMILIES` constant. Registering a predicate today gives you a schema and a template but no folder. ADR-028 decides that the predicate spec declares its own family via a `[path]` table, that the registry becomes the source of truth every consumer reads, that the business-graph predicate set ships in `starter/`, and that templates emit Obsidian wikilinks so the vault's graph view is the business graph. Task 38 is complete and committed as `c2a04fa` on main, not pushed. The largest refactor in the plan landed with the three original folders byte-identical.

**VERIFICATION REPORT**

| Claim | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rust workspace | `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` | 482 passed, 0 skipped |
| Format | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean |

| Plan | `compozy tasks validate --name ffs-mvp` | all tasks valid (48 scanned) |

All run after the final change. Verdict: PASS.

**What the filing cabinet now does**

- **Folders are data.** A predicate spec declares its own family in a `[path]` table, and every consumer reads the registry: renderer, materializer, fast-path watcher, search, a new `path.families` RPC, and the plugin, which loads the table at connect and keeps a last-known copy. The `widgets` fixture proves a fifth family needs only a TOML and a template.
- **Identity is opaque; names are data.** New entities get a 16-byte multibase id. The file name comes from the head atom's name field through a persisted path index, with `Sara_Chen_(City_Council).md` on collision and a `Moved to [[...]]` stub on rename. Old slug ids keep working.
- **The business graph exists.** Six new predicates and templates: orgs, articles, events, affiliations as their own role atoms, and the two identity assertions. A person's file renders its organization as a wikilink and an `## Affiliations` section by reverse lookup; an org renders `## People`. A merged entity renders a one-line stub.
- **Live check passed** on a scratch substrate: a hand-written org note became `orgs/by-name/A/Acme_Widgets.md` with an opaque id, and a person note naming it rendered a resolving link.

**Two things worth knowing**

- The live check needed one generic scribe addition: a hinted note whose frontmatter supplies the schema's required fields becomes a claim built from the schema's own keys. No predicate is named in code, and registering two new specs flipped two corpus fixtures from note fallback to real proposals on their own.
- The live output caught a real bug: a wikilink unquoted in YAML frontmatter parses as a nested list. It is now quoted, and editing that field routes to ingest rather than reverse-mapping a bracketed link into the claim.

Next in the build order is task 45, the multi-entity scribe and the three-outcome resolver, which now has both its inputs: the LLM engine and the identity layer.

# Task 45: Scribe v3 — multi-entity proposals + entity resolver (ADR-030, ADR-031)

## Overview
The newspaper goal turns one dropped article into many records: the article itself, the people it names, the organizations they belong to, the events it reports, and the roles that connect them. Each of those records may already exist in the substrate, so the scribe has to decide, per mention, whether it is looking at someone it knows, someone new, or someone it cannot tell apart from two candidates. This task is that clerk.

It is deliberately separate from task_36, and ordered after task_38, for two reasons. First, task_36 is the tracer bullet: it proves the extraction engines against the three starter predicates and gives the vault a readable daily digest weeks before any identity work exists. Second, the resolver needs things that only exist after task_38: opaque entity ids (`EntityId::mint`), the `affiliation`, `entity.same_as`, and `entity.different_from` predicates, the starter `config/resolution.toml`, and the path-to-entity index. It also needs real extraction output from task_36 and spike task_42 to set sensible weights and thresholds. Building the resolver before that evidence exists would mean tuning against guesses.

ADR-030 (`docs/research/2026-09-14-entity-resolution.md`) supplies the identity design: Fellegi-Sunter weights and two thresholds, three outcomes, aliases and priors that grow from accepted resolutions, merges as signed reversible atoms, and a NIL policy borrowed from Wikipedia's notability rule. ADR-031 (`docs/research/2026-09-14-top-level-ontologies.md`) supplies the shapes: a role is its own `affiliation` atom with a bearer, a context, and a temporal window; article mentions and event participants are entity references, not strings.

- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here

- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

- MUST support multi-entity extraction per submission (ADR-028): one article submission yields one `source.article` proposal plus N `person.generic`, M `org.company`, and K `event.business` proposals. Every proposal in the set MUST carry the article URL in provenance, and proposals MUST cross-reference each other by entity id (or display name when the id is not yet assigned) so the article's `mentions[]`, the event's `participants[]` and `source`, and the person's `organization` resolve to the same entities after acceptance. The proposals envelope on the skills-host wire MUST stay backward compatible (a single-proposal result is the degenerate case).
- MUST perform entity resolution on the daemon side before enqueueing (ADR-030): in `crates/ffs-daemon/src/scribe.rs`, a resolver that (a) blocks candidates by path family and a normalized name key; (b) generates candidates from `entity.search` v2 (`display_name`, `aliases[]`, prior count; task_40) and the store's `search_fts`, following `entity.same_as` chains so a mention matching a losing alias lands on the winner; (c) scores candidates with Fellegi-Sunter field weights on `organization`, `role`, and `location` agreement plus the prior, reading weights and the two thresholds from `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/resolution.toml` (starter file shipped by task_38, hot-reloaded like predicate specs); (d) treats any `entity.different_from` assertion as a hard block; (e) emits per proposal `resolution: "existing" | "new" | "ambiguous"` and `candidates: [{entity, score, matched_on}]`, where `ambiguous` covers scores between the thresholds or two candidates within a margin; (f) receives the whole multi-entity set for a submission so an org proposal in the same article can raise a person candidate already affiliated with it (coherence scoring itself is Phase 2; the interface ships now); (g) applies the NIL policy: `source.article`, `event.business`, and `org.company` always mint, a `person.generic` mints on first mention only with a distinguishing attribute (organization or role) or on a second sighting keyed by normalized name plus article organization context, otherwise the mention stays in the article's `mentions[]` with `entity` unset. Entity ids for `new` are opaque (16 random bytes, base58btc multibase, `EntityId::mint` from task_38), minted in the daemon's signing path at accept or auto-accept, never derived from a name. `resolution` and `candidates` are carried through quarantine storage and `ingest.list_pending` so the review UI can render a reconciliation picker and so task_39's additive-vs-conflict rule can act on them (`ambiguous` is always conflicting).
- MUST emit `affiliation` proposals (ADR-031) alongside person and org proposals whenever an article states or implies that a person holds a role at an organization: predicate `affiliation` with `person` (entity id or display name pending resolution), `organization` (same), `title`, `kind` (the ADR-031 enum), and `source` (the article URL); `valid_from` set to the stated role start when the article gives one, otherwise the article's `published_at`. - MUST grow aliases from accepted resolutions (ADR-030): when a proposal resolved to an existing entity is accepted or auto-accepted and its mention text differs from the entity's `display_name`, the mention text is appended to the entity's `aliases[]` as an additive edit. Priors for a surface form are the counts of accepted resolutions to each entity, read from the store, never cached in process memory.
- MUST extend the golden corpus with at least five business-press fixtures, paraphrased or synthetic per task_36's licensing rule: an executive hire, a funding round, an acquisition, a real-estate opening, and a profile piece, each paired with expected multi-entity proposals (article + people + orgs + events + affiliations) and each scored by the existing per-field precision/recall scorer.

- [ ] 45.1 Multi-entity proposal envelope + prompt rendering for every registered predicate, including ADR-028's `org.company`, `source.article`, `event.business`, and `person.generic` v2; cross-references between proposals in one set; wire shape stays backward compatible.
- [ ] 45.2 `resolution.toml` reader in the daemon (weights as m/u pairs, two thresholds, margin, blocking options; hot-reload alongside predicate specs).
- [ ] 45.3 Daemon-side resolver in `scribe.rs`: blocking, candidate generation via `entity.search` v2 + `search_fts`, `same_as` chain following, `different_from` hard block, scoring, three outcomes with `candidates[]`, whole-envelope input with the coherence hook; `resolution` and `candidates` carried through quarantine storage (task_29 tables) and `ingest.list_pending`.
- [ ] 45.4 NIL policy and opaque id minting in the signing path for `new`; second-sighting key; back-fill of the first mention when the second sighting mints.
- [ ] 45.5 `affiliation` proposals and object-shaped `mentions[]` / `participants[]` (ADR-031); role-ending as supersession proposals.
- [ ] 45.6 Alias growth on accept and auto-accept; store-backed priors; unit tests.

## Implementation Details
The engine seam, prompt builder, and schema validator from task_36 are reused unchanged; this task widens the envelope the engine returns and adds the daemon-side pass between the skill's output and the quarantine. The resolver is a pure function over (proposal set, candidate lookups, config) so it can be unit-tested with an in-memory store.

Resolution runs once per submission over the whole set, in dependency order: organizations first (they are the context for people), then people, then affiliations (which need both), then events and the article (which reference all of the above).

### Relevant Files
- `skills/scribe/` — envelope widening; affiliation emission; object-shaped mentions and participants.
- `skills/scribe/tests/corpus/` — new fixtures and the identity scorer.
- `crates/ffs-daemon/src/scribe.rs` — the resolver and its config reader.
- `crates/ffs-daemon/src/dispatch.rs` — minting on accept and auto-accept; alias growth.
- `crates/ffs-core/src/quarantine.rs` + `quarantine_sqlite.rs` — `resolution` and `candidates` columns.
- `crates/ffs-core/src/store/` — `resolve_same_as` helper (task_39 introduces it; reuse if present).
- `starter/config/resolution.toml` — shipped by task_38; consumed here.
- `obsidian-plugin/src/summary.ts` — `resolution` and `candidates` in the expanded proposal card (the picker itself is task_39).

### Dependent Files
- `crates/ffs-daemon/tests/ingest_pipeline_e2e.rs` — multi-entity e2e over a paraphrased article.
- `docs/onboarding/first-use-guide.md` — what "ambiguous" means and where it shows up.

### Related ADRs
- [ADR-030: Entity identity, resolution, and merge](adrs/adr-030.md) — opaque ids, the three-outcome resolver, `resolution.toml`, `same_as` / `different_from`, NIL policy, alias growth, identity scoring.
- [ADR-031](adrs/adr-031.md) — affiliation as its own role atom; object-shaped `mentions[]` / `participants[]`.
- [ADR-028](adrs/adr-028.md) — business-graph predicates the prompt builder renders; path families.
- [ADR-029](adrs/adr-029.md) — `ambiguous` is always conflicting; alias growth is additive.
- [ADR-026](adrs/adr-026.md) — engine seam and opt-in rule this task inherits.

## Deliverables
- Multi-entity proposal sets with cross-references and article provenance **(REQUIRED)**.
- Daemon-side three-outcome resolver (`resolution: existing | new | ambiguous` with `candidates[]`), driven by `resolution.toml`, honoring `same_as` and `different_from`, applying the NIL policy, minting opaque ids **(REQUIRED)**.
- `affiliation` proposals and object-shaped `mentions[]` / `participants[]` with entity ids **(REQUIRED)**.
- Alias growth from accepted resolutions; store-backed priors **(REQUIRED)**.
- Five business-press corpus fixtures scored per predicate, plus four identity fixtures scored with pairwise P/R and B-cubed **(REQUIRED)**.
- Unit tests with 80%+ coverage on new modules **(REQUIRED)**.

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - [ ] Multi-entity: the executive-hire fixture yields one `source.article`, one `person.generic`, one `org.company`, one `event.business` (`kind: hire`), and one `affiliation` proposal, all carrying the article URL in provenance and cross-referencing by entity id.
  - [ ] Three outcomes: a score above the upper threshold yields `existing`; below the lower yields `new`; between, or two candidates within the margin, yields `ambiguous` with a populated `candidates[]`; changing the thresholds in `resolution.toml` moves the outcome without a code change.
  - [ ] `same_as` and `different_from`: a mention matching an alias of a merged (losing) entity resolves to the winner; a candidate blocked by `different_from` is never returned as `existing`, even with a perfect name match.
  - [ ] NIL policy: a bare name with no distinguishing attribute stays in `mentions[]` with `entity` unset and mints on the second sighting with both mentions back-filled; an unknown person with an organization mints on first sighting.
  - [ ] Opaque ids: a `new` resolution yields, on accept, a base58btc multibase id that is not derived from the name.
  - [ ] Affiliation: a "stepped down" fixture yields a supersession proposal setting `valid_to` on the existing affiliation, not a new one.
  - [ ] Alias growth: accepting a proposal whose mention text was "S. Chen" for the entity displayed as "Sara Chen" appends "S. Chen" to her `aliases[]`; the prior for "S. Chen" then counts one.
  - [ ] Resolution order: organizations resolve before the people that reference them within one submission.
- Integration tests:
  - [ ] Multi-entity e2e over a paraphrased article: articles/, people/, orgs/ files land in the vault with wikilinks after accept.
  - [ ] `ingest.list_pending` exposes `resolution` and `candidates` on every proposal in a multi-entity set.
  - [ ] Identity scorer: pairwise precision/recall and B-cubed computed over the four identity fixtures; the wrong-merge-undo fixture restores both entities' clusters after the `same_as` atom is superseded.
- Test coverage target: >=80%
- All tests must pass

## Success Criteria
- The same person across three paraphrased articles, one using a nickname, resolves to one entity.
- Two people with the same name at different organizations stay separate.
- An ambiguous case produces a candidate list and routes to review; no Accept grant can auto-file it.
- All tests passing; coverage ≥80% on new modules; no copyrighted press text in git.

Wire conventions to implement (the daemon resolver, written by another fork, consumes exactly these; keep the envelope backward compatible: a single proposal with none of the new keys is still valid):
- Each proposal may carry `"local_ref": "<short stable token>"` assigned by the scribe within one submission (e.g. "org-1", "person-2", "event-1", "article"), unique per set.
- Cross-references between proposals in the same set use the DISPLAY NAME as printed, in these fields: `person.generic.claim.organization` (string display), `affiliation.claim.person` and `affiliation.claim.organization` (display strings), `source.article.claim.mentions[]` items `{display, context}` (no `entity` key from the scribe), `event.business.claim.participants[]` items `{display, role}`, `event.business.claim.source` (the article url). The daemon binds displays to proposals in the same set (case and whitespace insensitive) and later to entity ids; the scribe never invents ids.
- Affiliation proposals: predicate `affiliation`, claim `{person, organization, title, kind, source}` with kind from the ADR-031 enum [employee, executive, board, founder, investor, advisor, member, other], `source` = the article url, and top-level proposal `"valid_from": "<YYYY-MM-DD>"` when the article states a start date else the article's published_at; a role ending ("stepped down", "departs", "leaves") is emitted as an affiliation proposal with top-level `"ends_role": true` and `"valid_to": "<date>"` (the daemon turns it into a supersession of the matching existing affiliation head; the scribe never emits a new affiliation for an ending).

Keep the envelope contract `{"proposals": [...], "summary": "..."}` and add optional `"valid_from"`, `"valid_to"`, `"ends_role"`, `"local_ref"` per proposal.
2. llm.py: accept those per-proposal keys from the model (validate types; drop unknown keys), assign local_refs when the model omits them, carry them onto the wire proposal via make_proposal (extend make_proposal in engine.py with optional kwargs `local_ref`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `ends_role`, `extra_provenance`), and add the source_article provenance entry to every proposal in the set when an article url is known (from the article proposal's claim.url or the submission frontmatter). Also: after parsing, bind display references within the set (normalize case/whitespace) and record on each proposal `"refs": [{"field": "organization", "local_ref": "org-1"}, {"field": "mentions[2].entity", "local_ref": "person-1"}, ...]` for every display that matched another proposal in the set, so the daemon can rewrite them at accept without re-matching; unmatched displays get no ref entry. 3. engine.py apply_hint frontmatter path: unchanged semantics; add local_ref "hint" and the source_article provenance when the hint is an article with a url (small).
4. Corpus: five business-press fixtures (synthetic; invent names): 21-exec-hire (article + person + org + event kind hire + affiliation), 22-funding-round (org + investors as orgs + event funding with participants roles investor/investee + affiliations for named execs), 23-acquisition (two orgs, event acquisition with acquirer/target, an exec departure with ends_role), 24-real-estate-opening (org, event opening, a developer participant), 25-profile-piece (a person with two affiliations over time, one ended, aliases/nickname in prose). Each expected.json lists the multi-entity proposals with the fields that must match (predicate, key claim fields, kind enums, refs count), scored by the existing scorer; since the heuristic engine cannot produce these, mark them `engine: llm` in expected.json and make test_corpus.py skip llm-marked fixtures unless FFS_SCRIBE_ENGINE=llm and a backend is reachable (reuse score_llm.py's reachability check), while a deterministic unit test (test_multi_entity.py) feeds each fixture's canned model envelope (store it as `model_output.json` next to input.md) through LlmEngine with the FakeTransport and asserts the expected proposals, so the fixtures are exercised in CI without a network. Four identity fixtures (31-nickname-three-articles: three inputs in one fixture dir with model_output per article; 32-same-name-two-orgs; 33-rename-announced; 34-wrong-merge-undo) carry `expected_identity.json` describing the expected clustering as labels (e.g. mentions in article A and B are the same person "P1"; article C's "Sara Chen (City Council)" is "P2") for the Rust identity tests to consume; the Python side only checks the extraction and refs for them.
5. corpus_scorer.py: score refs (count of bound refs) and the new predicates' key fields; keep existing behavior.

Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/` bare and report the summary line, the exact wire keys added, and the fixture list with which are llm-only.

3. Store helpers on the `AtomStore` trait with default implementations built from existing methods where possible, and native SQL in `SqliteAtomStore` where a table is needed:
   - `fn same_as_target(&self, entity: &EntityId, as_of: Option<&Iso8601>) -> Result<Option<EntityId>, StoreError>`: the `target` of the head `entity.same_as` atom for `entity`, if any; and `fn follow_same_as(&self, entity: &EntityId, as_of) -> Result<EntityId, StoreError>` following chains with a cycle guard (max 16 hops) returning the final winner (or the input when none).
   - `fn different_from(&self, entity: &EntityId, as_of) -> Result<Vec<EntityId>, StoreError>`: all `other` ids from head `entity.different_from` atoms whose entity is `entity`, plus atoms where `other == entity` (symmetric; the second half needs a scan of `list_by_predicate("entity.different_from")`, fine at personal scale).
   - Priors table `resolution_priors(form TEXT, entity TEXT, count INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(form, entity))` in v5: `fn record_resolution(&self, form: &str, entity: &EntityId) -> Result<(), StoreError>` (increment) and `fn prior_counts(&self, form: &str) -> Result<Vec<(EntityId, u32)>, StoreError>` (descending). In-memory store keeps a HashMap.
   - NIL sightings table `nil_sightings(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, submission_id TEXT, display TEXT, first_seen TEXT)` in v5: `fn record_sighting(&self, key: &str, submission_id: &str, display: &str, when: &Iso8601) -> Result<Option<Sighting>, StoreError>` returning the PRIOR sighting if one existed (and leaving the row in place), `pub struct Sighting { pub key: String, pub submission_id: String, pub display: String, pub first_seen: Iso8601 }`, and `fn clear_sighting(&self, key: &str)`. In-memory equivalent.
   - `fn normalized_name_key(display: &str) -> String` as a free function in a new `ffs_core::resolve` module: lowercase, trim, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation except spaces and hyphens, strip common suffixes (jr, sr, ii, iii) and honorifics (mr, mrs, ms, dr) at the edges; and `fn surname_key(display: &str) -> String` (last token of the normalized form). Tests.
4. `resolution.rs` and the starter file: `Thresholds` gains `#[serde(default = "default_margin")] pub margin: f64` (default 1.0: two candidates whose scores are within `margin` are ambiguous); a new optional `[blocking]` table `BlockingConfig { #[serde(default = "default_true")] pub same_family: bool, #[serde(default)] pub key: BlockingKey }` with `enum BlockingKey { FullName, Surname }` default FullName; add both to starter/config/resolution.toml with comments; tests that the starter file still loads and margin defaults when absent.
5. Exports in lib.rs: `Candidate, CrossRef, Resolution, Sighting, BlockingConfig, BlockingKey, resolve::{normalized_name_key, surname_key}`.

Run `cargo nextest run -p ffs-core`, `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy -p ffs-core --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. The daemon will not compile until its fork adapts `Proposal { .. }` literals; that is expected. Report the summary line and the exact signatures added.

Python wire (being written concurrently by the scribe fork; parse leniently with serde defaults): per proposal optional `local_ref: String`, `refs: [{field: "organization" | "mentions[2].entity" | ..., local_ref}]`, `valid_from`, `valid_to` (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO), `ends_role: bool`, and a second provenance entry `{kind: "source_article", uri, hash_hex}`. 1. `resolver.rs`: a pure `resolve_set(set: &mut [Proposal], lookups: &dyn CandidateLookup, cfg: &ResolutionConfig, ctx: &SubmissionContext) -> ResolveReport` plus a `StoreLookup` implementing `CandidateLookup` over `&dyn AtomStore` + `&SpecRegistry`. Order: org.company first, then person.generic (and contact.person), then affiliation, then event.business, then source.article and everything else (derive the order from the refs graph: a proposal resolves after the proposals it references; fall back to that fixed predicate order). For each proposal whose family has a name field: (a) blocking: candidates only from the same family (cfg.blocking.same_family) and whose normalized name key (full name or surname per cfg.blocking.key) matches; (b) candidate generation: the store's entities for the family whose head `display_name`/name field or `aliases[]` match the key, plus `prior_counts(form)` entities, plus `search_fts(display)` hits mapped to entities; follow `follow_same_as` on every candidate so losers land on winners; dedupe; (c) scoring: sum over cfg.weights of agree/disagree for fields present on both sides: display_name exact normalized match, alias match, organization (compare the proposal's organization display, or the display of the org proposal it references in the same set, against the candidate's organization resolved to a display through the index or head claim), role, location, surname; prior adds `ln(1 + count)`; `matched_on` lists the agreeing fields; (d) `different_from(candidate)` containing any entity already bound in this set's context or listed in the proposal's refs excludes the candidate; also exclude a candidate that is `different_from` the top candidate when deciding a tie; (e) outcome: best >= auto_link and (second is None or best - second > margin) -> Existing with `entity` bound (after follow_same_as); best < review_floor or no candidates -> New; otherwise Ambiguous with candidates sorted by score desc (cap 5); Existing and Ambiguous fill `candidates`; (f) NIL policy: `source.article`, `event.business`, `org.company` always New when no candidate; a `person.generic` with no candidate and no distinguishing attribute (no organization ref/value, no role) stays unresolved: resolution None, and the resolver calls `record_sighting(key = normalized name + "|" + article org context)`; if a prior sighting exists, the person is New and the report lists `backfill: [(prior submission_id, display)]`; a person with an organization or role is New on first sighting; (g) when a person proposal is unresolved (bare name), the article's mentions item referencing it keeps `display` only (no entity), and the person proposal is dropped from the set with a warning in the report so it never reaches the quarantine as a mintable proposal. Wire it in main.rs around the SkillsHost extractor and give dispatcher tests a way to wrap their stubs.

4. `entity_search` gains `aliases` matching (a hit when the query matches any alias) and returns `matched_on: ["display_name"|"alias"]`; keep it small (task_40 does the rest).
5. Plugin: the expanded card shows `resolution: existing (Sara Chen)`, `resolution: new`, or `resolution: ambiguous` with the candidate list `display (score)`; vitest. Docs: first-use-guide gets one paragraph on what "ambiguous" means and that it always waits for you.
6. Tests: unit tests for the resolver with an in-memory store: three outcomes and that changing thresholds moves the outcome; margin tie -> ambiguous; same_as chain lands on the winner; different_from blocks a perfect name match; NIL bare name unresolved then minted on second sighting with backfill reported; person with org mints on first sighting; resolution order (org before person referencing it) and a bound org raising the person candidate; accept: ambiguous without choices errors, with choices binds; refs rewritten to ids (mentions entity set, organization is an id); ends_role supersedes the existing affiliation head with valid_to; alias growth appends "S. Chen" and prior_counts("s. chen") returns one for that entity; opaque id on New. Identity fixtures: read `skills/scribe/tests/corpus/3*/expected_identity.json` and `model_output*.json` written by the scribe fork if present (they may land after you start; write the test to skip with a clear message when absent, and to run when present): feed each article's canned proposals through resolve_set in sequence over one in-memory store (accepting after each), then compute pairwise precision/recall over same-entity pairs and B-cubed precision/recall over clusters versus the expected labels; the four fixtures are nickname-across-three-articles (one entity), same-name-two-orgs (two), rename-announced (one entity, alias grown), wrong-merge-undo (merge via a same_as atom then supersede it with valid_to; both clusters restored). Multi-entity e2e in tests/ingest_pipeline_e2e.rs or a new test: a stub scribe returning a canned multi-entity wire set through the ResolvingExtractor, accepted, lands articles/, people/, orgs/ files with wikilinks.

Verify: `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `npm test` in obsidian-plugin/. Report summary lines, the accept `choices` param shape, the resolver's public signature, and any ffs-core or skills change you needed but could not make.

14	The newspaper goal turns one dropped article into many records: the article itself, the people it names, the organizations they belong to, the events it reports, and the roles that connect them. Task 45 is complete and committed as `064e8f1` on main, not pushed. The "same person across fifty articles" question now has a working answer in code.

**VERIFICATION REPORT**

| Claim | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rust workspace | `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` | 513 passed, 0 skipped |
| Format | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean |

| Corpus | press-name grep | 0 files |
| Plan | `compozy tasks validate --name ffs-mvp` | all tasks valid (48 scanned) |

All run after the final change. Verdict: PASS.

**What the clerk does now**

- **One article becomes many records.** The scribe emits the article, its people, orgs, events, and affiliations as one set, cross-referenced by the names as printed. Every proposal carries the article's URL in provenance. The prompt learns these rules from the registry, so no predicate is named in code.
- **Every mention is resolved before it reaches you.** The daemon resolves the set in dependency order, orgs before the people who work there, with candidates drawn from names, aliases, store-backed priors, and full-text search. Scoring follows the weights in your `resolution.toml`, which hot-reloads. Merge chains are followed, "different people" assertions are hard blocks, and each proposal lands as existing, new, or ambiguous with its candidate list.
- **Ambiguous always waits for you.** Accepting a set with an unresolved ambiguity fails until a choice is supplied, which is the hook the task 39 picker will call.
- **Accept does the bookkeeping.** New entities get opaque ids, references are rewritten to those ids, a "stepped down" becomes a supersession with an end date, a differing mention text grows the entity's aliases, and each accepted link records a prior for next time.

**Identity harness results**, on synthetic fixtures with the owner's review picks simulated from the gold labels: 1.0 pairwise and B-cubed on all four. A nickname across three articles resolved to one person. Two same-name people at different orgs stayed ambiguous rather than auto-linked, which is the correct outcome and the one that caught a weight that had to change. A rename made the new name primary with the old as an alias. A wrong merge undone by superseding its atom restored both clusters.

**Two decisions to note.** The starter weights moved after the fixtures spoke: an exact name links on its own when nothing contradicts it, and a stated organization mismatch strongly opposes a link. The NIL policy applies only to bare names inside an article set, so contact cards and standalone person notes always mint.

**Follow-up carried**: an org's `## People` section can show a raw id until the org's next commit, because the materializer does not yet re-render entities referenced by a newly committed affiliation. That belongs with task 39 or 40.

Next in the build order is task 40, the courier.

3. Implement the task.

# Task 40: Courier: deterministic email-and-feeds intake + ffs_search v2 + URL dedup (publisher policy in sources.toml)

## Overview
Reshaped 2026-09-14 per ADR-035 and spike task_43; amended 2026-09-15 per the ADR-035 amendment. The courier is the deterministic, scheduled half of the newspaper goal. What it does with each publisher is the owner's policy in `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/sources.toml` (`intake = pointer | clip`, `fetch = off | session | scheduled`), never a refusal in code: the software records the publishers' terms (spike task_43) and complies with the owner's setting. The starter file sets bizjournals.com, the Charlotte Observer, and Axios Charlotte to `pointer` / `session`, so by default the courier files their headlines and URLs and leaves the reading to the owner-present morning read (task_48); the owner may set `clip` or `scheduled` and the courier complies. What the courier does:

- **The owner's own mailbox.** Under the starter defaults the Charlotte Business Journal digest is decoded into `source.article` pointers: title, url (recovered from the base64 path of each `link.bizjournals.com/click/...` tracking link, no click), date, publication, no content. CLTtoday items (6AM City, personal-use license; `intake = "clip"`, `fetch = "off"` because the blurb is the body) are filed with their blurb text and the parenthetical attribution each item carries ("(Charlotte Business Journal)", "(WBTV)"), which goes into provenance as `reported_by` so ADR-034's quorum can discount an item that is itself a copy of another outlet's report. The mailbox is a Google Workspace account; 40.3 decides OAuth versus an app password, with the secret in the OS keychain either way.
- **Public-record and permitted feeds**, found by the task_43 probe: the Mecklenburg County permits ArcGIS FeatureServer (`AccelaAllPermits`, REST JSON, no key), the Charlotte City Council Legistar Web API (JSON, no token, 1,000-row cap), SEC EDGAR full-text search and submissions (declared `User-Agent`, 10 requests per second ceiling, no crawling), and newsroom RSS (Duke Energy, Truist). Each is an adapter that writes ingest files under the same contract.

An LLM is not needed to move text from an email or a JSON feed into a folder; extraction is the scribe's job (task_36), identity is the resolver's (task_45). So the courier is an FFS skill bundle, `skills/courier/`, the fourth agent ADR-009 named. It is stdlib-only Python like the auditor: `imaplib` and `email` for the mailbox, `urllib` for the feeds and for any publisher the owner set to `fetch = "scheduled"`, `json` and `xml.etree` for their payloads, credentials and any owner-exported session cookies from the OS keychain per task_27, run on a daemon schedule like the auditor. It has no LLM client. The scheduled-fetch path exists (40.11) but is disabled for terms-restricted publishers by the starter `sources.toml`.

An agent host (Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code) may run the same contract: `docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md` stays as that statement and a worked example, nothing more. The morning read, where an assistant opens articles one at a time with the owner present and clips on cue, is task_48 and is not part of the courier.

Three gaps this task closes are unchanged from the original scope. There is no published ingest shape for an article, so the scribe guesses from free text and the engines have no stable `predicate:` hint or `## Mentions` section to do multi-entity extraction reliably. Nothing deduplicates by URL, so a re-read files a second article. And `entity.search` matches only the hardcoded `display_name` / `title` field, so `ffs_search "Acme"` cannot find an org filed under its alias, which makes the convention's search-before-write loop (ADR-027) too weak for a graph with aliases.

Amended 2026-09-14 (ADR-030, ADR-031). Entity ids are opaque and permanent (ADR-030), so the courier never supplies ids and the article's `<publication>-<date>-<title>` slug is a projection basename and a resolver blocking key, not the identity; the dedup keys are the normalized `url` and an optional `content_hash`. Mentions and event participants are entity references, not names (ADR-031): `## Mentions` bullets become `{entity, display, context}` items and `## Events` bullets carry participants with a role in the event, with `entity` filled in by the resolver. `entity.search` v2 is the resolver's candidate generator with the Wikidata and Fellegi-Sunter lessons built in: it ranks by exact name, alias, prior count, then full-text rank; it follows `entity.same_as` chains; it excludes anything the caller's context is `different_from`; and it exposes the reconciliation shape (query, candidates with score and `matched_on`) that a W3C Reconciliation Service facade could wrap later.

<critical>
- ALWAYS READ the PRD and TechSpec before starting
- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here
- FOCUS ON "WHAT" — describe what needs to be accomplished, not how
- MINIMIZE CODE — show code only to illustrate current structure or problem areas
- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

<requirements>
- MUST ship the courier as a daemon-hosted skill bundle `skills/courier/` per ADR-009: `SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name: courier`, `kind: courier`, `entry_point: courier.py`, `python: python3`, `timeout_ms`, and a `schedule` (cron-style or interval; the daemon's scheduler from task_41 subtask 41.3 drives it, and until that lands `ffs courier run` invokes one tick by hand); `definition.atom.json`; `courier.py`; `adapters/` (one module per source); `tests/`. Zero pip dependencies: `imaplib`, `email`, `urllib.request`, `json`, `xml.etree`, `hashlib`, `tomllib`, and the `ffs_skill` helper only. The bundle MUST NOT contain an LLM client or a browser driver; extraction is the scribe's. A cookie jar exists only in the scheduled-fetch path (40.11), loaded from keychain-stored cookies the owner exported explicitly, and is used only for publishers the owner set to `fetch = "scheduled"` (ADR-035 as amended 2026-09-15).
- MUST read configuration from `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/courier.toml` (seeded by the installer from `starter/config/courier.toml`) with environment overrides: `[mailbox]` host, port, folder, `auth` (`oauth | app_password`), `mark_seen` (bool), and a `[[mailbox.source]]` list, each with `sender` (from-address or domain), `subject_filter` (optional regex), and `publisher` (a key into `sources.toml`, which supplies `intake` and `fetch`; a source with no matching publisher entry is filed as `pointer` and logged); `[[feed]]` entries, each with `adapter` (`meck_permits | charlotte_legistar | sec_edgar | rss`), its endpoint or feed url, a `since` watermark, `publication`, and adapter-specific filters (permit type and minimum declared cost; Legistar body ids; EDGAR form types and a company list; RSS nothing); `[edgar]` `user_agent` (required, declared per the SEC fair-access policy) and `max_rps` (default 8, hard ceiling 10); `[output]` digest title prefix. Secrets MUST NOT live in TOML: the mailbox token or app password comes from the OS keychain (service `ffs.courier.<host>`, via the task_27 keyring helpers exposed through `ffs_skill`) or from `FFS_COURIER_MAIL_PASSWORD` for tests, never from config or argv.
- MUST read per-publisher policy from `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/sources.toml` (seeded by the installer from `starter/config/sources.toml`; owner-edited; git-versioned; hot-reloaded by the daemon like predicate specs): one `[[publisher]]` table per publisher with `key`, `name`, `domains` (list), `intake = "pointer" | "clip"` (what the courier files from a mailbox item: title, url, and date only, or also the body when the item carries one), `fetch = "off" | "session" | "scheduled"` (off: never fetch; session: fetch only during an owner-present morning read on the owner's cue, task_48; scheduled: the courier may fetch the articles named in the owner's own digest at a human pace and never crawl beyond them), and for `scheduled` a `daily_cap` (default 20) and `min_pause_seconds` (default 8). The starter file ships bizjournals.com, charlotteobserver.com, and axios.com at `pointer` / `session` with a comment saying where their terms are recorded (spike task_43) and that the setting is the owner's; CLTtoday at `clip` / `off`; the public-record feeds at `clip` / `scheduled`. The loader MUST validate the enums and reject unknown keys with a clear error, MUST NOT contain any domain denylist or allowlist, and MUST apply the owner's values as written: the software does not adjudicate the owner's license or fair-use position (ADR-035 amendment, 2026-09-15). A loader test covers each enum value, an unknown key, and the starter file.
- MUST implement the scheduled-fetch path (40.11) for publishers whose `fetch = "scheduled"`: after the mailbox tick, for each new pointer whose publisher is `scheduled`, fetch that URL once with `urllib` using the owner's exported session cookies from the keychain (service `ffs.courier.cookies.<domain>`; the export is a documented manual step in the first-use guide), then pause for a randomized interval of at least `min_pause_seconds`, stop at `daily_cap` per publisher per day, request only URLs decoded from the owner's own digest (never a listing, index, or search page; never a link found inside a fetched page), log every request in the tick result and the courier ledger, and on success rewrite that item's ingest file with the article body as a `clip` (`intake` for that item becomes `clip`, `content_hash` computed from the page bytes). Spike task_43 found that bizjournals.com answers 403 to non-browser clients even with a browser User-Agent, so this stdlib path MAY still fail against a bot wall; on any non-200 the item stays a pointer, the failure is counted in `fetch_failures`, and the documented fallback is a browser-hosted fetch during the morning read (`fetch = "session"`). This path is implemented and tested in this task and is disabled for terms-restricted publishers by the starter `sources.toml`.
- MUST implement one mailbox tick as: connect, select the folder, find unseen messages matching each source's sender and subject filters, and for each message parse the HTML or text body into items (headline, blurb, link) using `email` and `html.parser`; decode `link.bizjournals.com/click/<campaign>/<base64url>/...` and similar tracking wrappers into the real URL before normalization (a table of known wrappers, extensible in `courier.toml`); normalize every link per the URL rule below; skip any item whose normalized URL already appears in the courier's local ledger (`$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/seen.json`, keyed by normalized URL with the date first seen) or in the substrate (an `entity.search` call with `predicate: source.article` and the URL); write one ingest file per new item per the intake contract, with `intake` set from the publisher's `sources.toml` entry (`pointer`: title, url, date, empty body; `clip`: also the item's body when the mailbox carries one); write or append the day's digest note; update the ledger; mark the message seen only when every item's file was written. A second tick over the same message MUST write zero new files.
- MUST implement one feed tick per configured `[[feed]]`: call the adapter with the `since` watermark, map each new record to an ingest file (a permit becomes an `event.business` proposal of kind `opening`, `expansion`, or `other` with the owner entity and declared cost as `amount` and the permit number in provenance; a Legistar matter becomes an `event.business` or a `note` with petitioner names as `## Mentions` and the meeting date; an EDGAR 8-K item 5.02 becomes an `affiliation` hint with the officer and company; an RSS release becomes a `source.article` with `intake: clip` and the publisher as `reported_by`), advance the watermark only after every file was written, and respect each source's published rate limit (EDGAR: declared `User-Agent`, at most `max_rps` requests per second, no crawling beyond the query). 72	## Implementation Details
73	Current structure: `crates/ffs-daemon/src/ingest_watcher.rs` submits any eligible `.md` under `ingest/` after the stability window and moves it to `processed/`; `crates/ffs-daemon/src/scribe.rs` translates skill proposals into quarantine `Proposal`s; `skills/scribe/extraction.py` parses frontmatter tolerantly (`parse_markdown`) but only consults `name` / `title` / `email` / `phone` / `org` keys and never a `predicate` hint. `skills/auditor/` is the shape to copy for the courier: `SKILL.md` frontmatter with `kind`, `entry_point`, `python`, `timeout_ms`; `audit.py` importing `query`, `log`, `run` from `skills/_lib/ffs_skill.py`; `tests/conftest.py` doing its own `sys.path` setup. The skills host discovers bundles under `$FFS_DATA_DIR/skills/` and the daemon spawns them by name (`crates/ffs-daemon/src/main.rs`); the auditor has no periodic driver today, which task_41 subtask 41.3 adds and this task reuses.
74	
75	`entity.search` in `crates/ffs-daemon/src/dispatch.rs` iterates `registry.names()`, lists atoms per predicate, and substring-matches one hardcoded field (`title` for `note`, else `display_name`); the predicate registry already exposes each spec's `claim_schema`, which is where the v2 field list comes from. The `AtomStore` trait already has `search_fts(query, limit)` (FTS5 MATCH over claim payloads, returning content hashes) that no RPC exposes; the FTS tier of v2 is that method plus a hash-to-entity lookup and a capability filter. Prior counts come from accepted proposals: each accept that resolved a surface form to an entity is visible as an atom whose provenance carries the mention text, so the count is a store query, not new state.
76	
77	Because entity ids are opaque under ADR-030, the resolver's blocking key for articles is the `<publication>-<date>-<title>` slug and the dedup keys are normalized `url` and `content_hash`; the same slug with a different `url` is two articles, the same `url` with a different title is one.
78	
79	The contract is deliberately a superset of what the heuristic engine can consume: with `FFS_SCRIBE_ENGINE=heuristic` the `predicate:` hint plus structured `## Mentions` bullets yield correct proposals without an LLM, so the courier path works on a fresh install; the `llm` engine improves extraction quality for the summary body and fills `## Mentions` in email-only mode.
80	
81	Why a bundle and not an agent: the mailbox, the filters, the feeds, and the files are deterministic, and a deterministic step is testable with fixtures in CI, restartable, and auditable in the daily summary. An agent doing the same job adds a model call and a host process to the first link of a daily chain, and neither makes the files better. Reading the articles behind the pointers is a different activity with a different rule: the owner present, one at a time, at human pace (ADR-035, task_48). The courier's job ends at the pointer.
82	
83	Persistence-honesty vocabulary for both couriers (mirrors ADR-027): *submitted* (file dropped, watcher will pick it up), *proposed* (in quarantine), *filed* (accepted atom, visible in the vault), *auto-filed* (accepted by an ADR-029 policy). The bundle's tick result and the skill use exactly these words.
