# Task 40: Courier: deterministic email-and-feeds intake + ffs_search v2 + URL dedup (publisher policy in sources.toml)

## Overview
Reshaped 2026-09-14 per ADR-035 and spike task_43; amended 2026-09-15 per the ADR-035 amendment. The courier is the deterministic, scheduled half of the newspaper goal. What it does with each publisher is the owner's policy in `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/sources.toml` (`intake = pointer | clip`, `fetch = off | session | scheduled`), never a refusal in code: the software records the publishers' terms (spike task_43) and complies with the owner's setting. The starter file sets bizjournals.com, the Charlotte Observer, and Axios Charlotte to `pointer` / `session`, so by default the courier files their headlines and URLs and leaves the reading to the owner-present morning read (task_48); the owner may set `clip` or `scheduled` and the courier complies. What the courier does:

- **The owner's own mailbox.** Under the starter defaults the Charlotte Business Journal digest is decoded into `source.article` pointers: title, url (recovered from the base64 path of each `link.bizjournals.com/click/...` tracking link, no click), date, publication, no content. CLTtoday items (6AM City, personal-use license; `intake = "clip"`, `fetch = "off"` because the blurb is the body) are filed with their blurb text and the parenthetical attribution each item carries ("(Charlotte Business Journal)", "(WBTV)"), which goes into provenance as `reported_by` so ADR-034's quorum can discount an item that is itself a copy of another outlet's report. The mailbox is a Google Workspace account; 40.3 decides OAuth versus an app password, with the secret in the OS keychain either way.
- **Public-record and permitted feeds**, found by the task_43 probe: the Mecklenburg County permits ArcGIS FeatureServer (`AccelaAllPermits`, REST JSON, no key), the Charlotte City Council Legistar Web API (JSON, no token, 1,000-row cap), SEC EDGAR full-text search and submissions (declared `User-Agent`, 10 requests per second ceiling, no crawling), and newsroom RSS (Duke Energy, Truist). Each is an adapter that writes ingest files under the same contract.

An LLM is not needed to move text from an email or a JSON feed into a folder; extraction is the scribe's job (task_36), identity is the resolver's (task_45). So the courier is an FFS skill bundle, `skills/courier/`, the fourth agent ADR-009 named. It is stdlib-only Python like the auditor: `imaplib` and `email` for the mailbox, `urllib` for the feeds and for any publisher the owner set to `fetch = "scheduled"`, `json` and `xml.etree` for their payloads, credentials and any owner-exported session cookies from the OS keychain per task_27, run on a daemon schedule like the auditor. It has no LLM client. The scheduled-fetch path exists (40.11) but is disabled for terms-restricted publishers by the starter `sources.toml`.

An agent host (Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code) may run the same contract: `docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md` stays as that statement and a worked example, nothing more. The morning read, where an assistant opens articles one at a time with the owner present and clips on cue, is task_48 and is not part of the courier.

Three gaps this task closes are unchanged from the original scope. There is no published ingest shape for an article, so the scribe guesses from free text and the engines have no stable `predicate:` hint or `## Mentions` section to do multi-entity extraction reliably. Nothing deduplicates by URL, so a re-read files a second article. And `entity.search` matches only the hardcoded `display_name` / `title` field, so `ffs_search "Acme"` cannot find an org filed under its alias, which makes the convention's search-before-write loop (ADR-027) too weak for a graph with aliases.

Amended 2026-09-14 (ADR-030, ADR-031). Entity ids are opaque and permanent (ADR-030), so the courier never supplies ids and the article's `<publication>-<date>-<title>` slug is a projection basename and a resolver blocking key, not the identity; the dedup keys are the normalized `url` and an optional `content_hash`. Mentions and event participants are entity references, not names (ADR-031): `## Mentions` bullets become `{entity, display, context}` items and `## Events` bullets carry participants with a role in the event, with `entity` filled in by the resolver. `entity.search` v2 is the resolver's candidate generator with the Wikidata and Fellegi-Sunter lessons built in: it ranks by exact name, alias, prior count, then full-text rank; it follows `entity.same_as` chains; it excludes anything the caller's context is `different_from`; and it exposes the reconciliation shape (query, candidates with score and `matched_on`) that a W3C Reconciliation Service facade could wrap later.

<critical>
- ALWAYS READ the PRD and TechSpec before starting
- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here
- FOCUS ON "WHAT" — describe what needs to be accomplished, not how
- MINIMIZE CODE — show code only to illustrate current structure or problem areas
- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

<requirements>
- MUST ship the courier as a daemon-hosted skill bundle `skills/courier/` per ADR-009: `SKILL.md` with frontmatter `name: courier`, `kind: courier`, `entry_point: courier.py`, `python: python3`, `timeout_ms`, and a `schedule` (cron-style or interval; the daemon's scheduler from task_41 subtask 41.3 drives it, and until that lands `ffs courier run` invokes one tick by hand); `definition.atom.json`; `courier.py`; `adapters/` (one module per source); `tests/`. Zero pip dependencies: `imaplib`, `email`, `urllib.request`, `json`, `xml.etree`, `hashlib`, `tomllib`, and the `ffs_skill` helper only. The bundle MUST NOT contain an LLM client or a browser driver; extraction is the scribe's. A cookie jar exists only in the scheduled-fetch path (40.11), loaded from keychain-stored cookies the owner exported explicitly, and is used only for publishers the owner set to `fetch = "scheduled"` (ADR-035 as amended 2026-09-15).
- MUST read configuration from `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/courier.toml` (seeded by the installer from `starter/config/courier.toml`) with environment overrides: `[mailbox]` host, port, folder, `auth` (`oauth | app_password`), `mark_seen` (bool), and a `[[mailbox.source]]` list, each with `sender` (from-address or domain), `subject_filter` (optional regex), and `publisher` (a key into `sources.toml`, which supplies `intake` and `fetch`; a source with no matching publisher entry is filed as `pointer` and logged); `[[feed]]` entries, each with `adapter` (`meck_permits | charlotte_legistar | sec_edgar | rss`), its endpoint or feed url, a `since` watermark, `publication`, and adapter-specific filters (permit type and minimum declared cost; Legistar body ids; EDGAR form types and a company list; RSS nothing); `[edgar]` `user_agent` (required, declared per the SEC fair-access policy) and `max_rps` (default 8, hard ceiling 10); `[output]` digest title prefix. Secrets MUST NOT live in TOML: the mailbox token or app password comes from the OS keychain (service `ffs.courier.<host>`, via the task_27 keyring helpers exposed through `ffs_skill`) or from `FFS_COURIER_MAIL_PASSWORD` for tests, never from config or argv.
- MUST read per-publisher policy from `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/sources.toml` (seeded by the installer from `starter/config/sources.toml`; owner-edited; git-versioned; hot-reloaded by the daemon like predicate specs): one `[[publisher]]` table per publisher with `key`, `name`, `domains` (list), `intake = "pointer" | "clip"` (what the courier files from a mailbox item: title, url, and date only, or also the body when the item carries one), `fetch = "off" | "session" | "scheduled"` (off: never fetch; session: fetch only during an owner-present morning read on the owner's cue, task_48; scheduled: the courier may fetch the articles named in the owner's own digest at a human pace and never crawl beyond them), and for `scheduled` a `daily_cap` (default 20) and `min_pause_seconds` (default 8). The starter file ships bizjournals.com, charlotteobserver.com, and axios.com at `pointer` / `session` with a comment saying where their terms are recorded (spike task_43) and that the setting is the owner's; CLTtoday at `clip` / `off`; the public-record feeds at `clip` / `scheduled`. The loader MUST validate the enums and reject unknown keys with a clear error, MUST NOT contain any domain denylist or allowlist, and MUST apply the owner's values as written: the software does not adjudicate the owner's license or fair-use position (ADR-035 amendment, 2026-09-15). A loader test covers each enum value, an unknown key, and the starter file.
- MUST implement the scheduled-fetch path (40.11) for publishers whose `fetch = "scheduled"`: after the mailbox tick, for each new pointer whose publisher is `scheduled`, fetch that URL once with `urllib` using the owner's exported session cookies from the keychain (service `ffs.courier.cookies.<domain>`; the export is a documented manual step in the first-use guide), then pause for a randomized interval of at least `min_pause_seconds`, stop at `daily_cap` per publisher per day, request only URLs decoded from the owner's own digest (never a listing, index, or search page; never a link found inside a fetched page), log every request in the tick result and the courier ledger, and on success rewrite that item's ingest file with the article body as a `clip` (`intake` for that item becomes `clip`, `content_hash` computed from the page bytes). Spike task_43 found that bizjournals.com answers 403 to non-browser clients even with a browser User-Agent, so this stdlib path MAY still fail against a bot wall; on any non-200 the item stays a pointer, the failure is counted in `fetch_failures`, and the documented fallback is a browser-hosted fetch during the morning read (`fetch = "session"`). This path is implemented and tested in this task and is disabled for terms-restricted publishers by the starter `sources.toml`.
- MUST implement one mailbox tick as: connect, select the folder, find unseen messages matching each source's sender and subject filters, and for each message parse the HTML or text body into items (headline, blurb, link) using `email` and `html.parser`; decode `link.bizjournals.com/click/<campaign>/<base64url>/...` and similar tracking wrappers into the real URL before normalization (a table of known wrappers, extensible in `courier.toml`); normalize every link per the URL rule below; skip any item whose normalized URL already appears in the courier's local ledger (`$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/seen.json`, keyed by normalized URL with the date first seen) or in the substrate (an `entity.search` call with `predicate: source.article` and the URL); write one ingest file per new item per the intake contract, with `intake` set from the publisher's `sources.toml` entry (`pointer`: title, url, date, empty body; `clip`: also the item's body when the mailbox carries one); write or append the day's digest note; update the ledger; mark the message seen only when every item's file was written. A second tick over the same message MUST write zero new files.
- MUST implement one feed tick per configured `[[feed]]`: call the adapter with the `since` watermark, map each new record to an ingest file (a permit becomes an `event.business` proposal of kind `opening`, `expansion`, or `other` with the owner entity and declared cost as `amount` and the permit number in provenance; a Legistar matter becomes an `event.business` or a `note` with petitioner names as `## Mentions` and the meeting date; an EDGAR 8-K item 5.02 becomes an `affiliation` hint with the officer and company; an RSS release becomes a `source.article` with `intake: clip` and the publisher as `reported_by`), advance the watermark only after every file was written, and respect each source's published rate limit (EDGAR: declared `User-Agent`, at most `max_rps` requests per second, no crawling beyond the query). Feed payload samples are public record and MAY be committed as test fixtures; newsletter text MUST NOT be.
- MUST provide a dry-run mode (`FFS_COURIER_DRY_RUN=1` or `ffs courier run --dry-run`) that performs every step but writes ingest files and the digest to a scratch directory (`$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/dry-run/<timestamp>/`) and does not mark messages seen or update the ledger; the tick's result JSON lists the files it would have written.
- MUST publish the article ingest contract in `docs/agent-memory/CONVENTION.md` (new section) and in both courier skills: one markdown file per article in `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/` with YAML frontmatter `predicate: source.article`, `title`, `url` (both required), `publication`, `published_at` (ISO 8601 date), `byline`, `tags` (list), `intake` (`pointer | clip | feed | morning_read`), optional `reported_by` (the outlet a newsletter item attributes, so ADR-034 counts it as a copy of that outlet, not an independent source), and optional `content_hash` (multibase-encoded digest, supplied only by feed adapters that receive the full record; ADR-031's information-bearer key); a body that is empty for `pointer`, the newsletter blurb or the article body for `clip` (what the owner's `sources.toml` policy allowed the courier to file, or what the owner clipped during the read), the record's own summary field for `feed`, and the owner's note for `morning_read`; clipped bodies carry classification tier `clip` per ADR-035 so they are never federated unless a capability names the tier; a `## Mentions` section of bullets `- <Name> — <one-line role/org context>` for people and organizations, where each bullet becomes one `mentions[]` item `{entity, display, context}` with `display` and `context` taken verbatim from the bullet and `entity` filled in by task_45's resolver (the courier never supplies entity ids, per ADR-030); an optional `## Events` section of bullets `- <kind>: <one-line description> | <Name> (<role-in-event>), <Name> (<role-in-event>)` using the `event.business` kinds from ADR-028 and the participant roles from ADR-031, where each named participant becomes a `participants[]` item `{entity, display, role}` resolved the same way. For `pointer` items `## Mentions` is absent; for `clip` items the courier leaves it empty and the scribe's engine fills it from the body; for `feed` items the adapter MAY pre-fill it from the record's structured fields (permit owner, petitioner, officer name), marked with a `courier-structured` tag so the scribe treats them as high-confidence hints rather than free-text guesses. The scribe MUST truncate any body over a configurable limit (default 4 000 characters) and attach a `parse-warning` rationale so the truncation is visible in the quarantine.
- MUST make the scribe honor an explicit `predicate:` frontmatter hint: when present and registered, the primary proposal uses that predicate (validated against its `claim_schema` as today); an unregistered hint falls back to the current inference path with a warning. `## Mentions` bullets become `person.generic` / `org.company` proposals (task_36's multi-entity path); `## Events` bullets become `event.business` proposals with `participants[]` objects; every secondary proposal carries the article's URL in its provenance and the article's entity id in its `mentions[]` / `sources` field per ADR-028, and the article proposal's `mentions[]` and the event proposals' `participants[]` carry the resolver's chosen entity id per item (or no `entity` when the resolver answered `new` or `ambiguous`, in which case the proposal routes to review per ADR-029 and the id is back-filled on accept).
- MUST deduplicate articles by normalized URL. Normalization (stdlib only, in `skills/_lib/urlnorm.py`, shared by courier and scribe): lowercase scheme and host, strip `utm_*` / `fbclid` / `gclid` / `mc_cid` / `mc_eid` query params, drop fragments, collapse a trailing slash. Per ADR-030 the article's entity id is opaque and minted once; `<publication-slug>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<title-slug>` is the projection basename and the resolver's blocking key, never the identity. task_45's resolver MUST match `source.article` on normalized `url` first and on `content_hash` second (when both submissions carry one), so a changed title on re-read still updates the existing entity (a supersession) rather than creating a sibling, and a re-fetch of the same page is a second bearer of the same content, not a second article. Both submissions' provenance MUST survive on the chain.
- MUST write the daily digest: one `note` per publication per day titled `<publication> digest YYYY-MM-DD` whose `## References` section lists every article filed that day as a `[[target|display]]` wikilink (target is the article's unique projection basename, display is its title, per ADR-030's naming rule); a second tick on the same day appends to the existing digest file in `ingest/` if it has not been consumed yet, or writes a new note that the resolver merges into the day's digest entity by title. The scribe MUST populate the note's `references[]` from those bullets (the field exists in `starter/predicates/note.toml`; today the scribe does not fill it). The digest note is how "did I read the paper end to end?" is answered from the vault.

The skills host discovers bundles under `$FFS_DATA_DIR/skills/` and the daemon spawns them by name (`crates/ffs-daemon/src/main.rs`); the auditor has no periodic driver today, which task_41 subtask 41.3 adds and this task reuses.

`entity.search` in `crates/ffs-daemon/src/dispatch.rs` iterates `registry.names()`, lists atoms per predicate, and substring-matches one hardcoded field (`title` for `note`, else `display_name`); the predicate registry already exposes each spec's `claim_schema`, which is where the v2 field list comes from. The `AtomStore` trait already has `search_fts(query, limit)` (FTS5 MATCH over claim payloads, returning content hashes) that no RPC exposes; the FTS tier of v2 is that method plus a hash-to-entity lookup and a capability filter. Prior counts come from accepted proposals: each accept that resolved a surface form to an entity is visible as an atom whose provenance carries the mention text, so the count is a store query, not new state.

Because entity ids are opaque under ADR-030, the resolver's blocking key for articles is the `<publication>-<date>-<title>` slug and the dedup keys are normalized `url` and `content_hash`; the same slug with a different `url` is two articles, the same `url` with a different title is one.

The contract is deliberately a superset of what the heuristic engine can consume: with `FFS_SCRIBE_ENGINE=heuristic` the `predicate:` hint plus structured `## Mentions` bullets yield correct proposals without an LLM, so the courier path works on a fresh install; the `llm` engine improves extraction quality for the summary body and fills `## Mentions` in email-only mode.

Why a bundle and not an agent: the mailbox, the filters, the feeds, and the files are deterministic, and a deterministic step is testable with fixtures in CI, restartable, and auditable in the daily summary. An agent doing the same job adds a model call and a host process to the first link of a daily chain, and neither makes the files better. Reading the articles behind the pointers is a different activity with a different rule: the owner present, one at a time, at human pace (ADR-035, task_48). The courier's job ends at the pointer.

Persistence-honesty vocabulary for both couriers (mirrors ADR-027): *submitted* (file dropped, watcher will pick it up), *proposed* (in quarantine), *filed* (accepted atom, visible in the vault), *auto-filed* (accepted by an ADR-029 policy). The bundle's tick result and the skill use exactly these words.

Task 40 is grounded. It is consistent with ADR-035 as amended, ADR-030, and ADR-031; two conventions the task leaves open, I'm pinning now so four forks can build concurrently: mailbox auth is an app password held in the keychain (Google Workspace OAuth device flow is not a stdlib job; documented as later), and the courier reports its last tick by writing `ingest/.courier/last_run.json`, which the daemon's health summary reads, so no new daemon state is needed. Pre-change signal: no `skills/courier/`, no URL normalizer, `entity.search` matches one name field, no courier verb.

**Execution checklist (task 40)**
1. Article ingest contract in CONVENTION.md; both courier skills and the scribe agree on it byte for byte.
2. URL normalization in Python and Rust with a shared fixture; article basename slug; content hash prefixes.
3. Courier bundle: mailbox tick with pointer and clip intake per `sources.toml`, tracking-link decoding, ledger, digest note, mark-seen, dry run, keychain-only secrets, starter `courier.toml` and `sources.toml` with a loader that has no domain lists.
4. Four feed adapters with public-record fixtures, watermarks, and the EDGAR rate limiter.
5. Scribe: mentions and events bullets into proposals with object items, body truncation with a parse warning, references from bullets, courier-structured hints, frontmatter round-trip.
6. Resolver: articles matched by normalized URL then content hash; mentions and participants get entity ids.
7. `entity.search` v2: schema-declared fields, FTS tier, filters, path, matched_on, score, four-tier ordering, same_as following, different_from exclusion; `ffs_search` schema updated.
8. `health.summary.courier`, auditor line and missed-schedule flag, `ffs courier run|status`, installer wiring.
9. Scheduled-fetch path: digest URLs only, human pace, daily cap, cookies from keychain, clip rewrite on success, pointer kept on failure, starter policy never triggers it for the three publishers.
10. Docs: courier section in the first-use guide, README listing, agent-hosted skill reframed with the bundle's exact example.
11. Live dry run on one real digest email; full verification across toolchains.

input.description: task_40 F1: courier bundle + adapters
input.prompt:
You own the courier skill bundle of task_40 (read .compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/task_40.md in full, adr-035 with its amendment, adr-009, skills/auditor/ as the shape to copy, skills/_lib/ffs_skill.py, and docs/research/spikes/task-43-intake-reality.md for the real digest shape). Files you own: skills/courier/** (new: SKILL.md, definition.atom.json, courier.py, config.py, mailbox.py, ledger.py, writer.py, fetch.py, adapters/{meck_permits,charlotte_legistar,sec_edgar,rss}.py, tests/** with synthetic .eml fixtures and public-record JSON/XML fixtures), skills/_lib/urlnorm.py (new), skills/_lib/fixtures/urlnorm.json (new shared fixture: a list of {raw, normalized} pairs the Rust side also consumes), skills/_lib/ffs_skill.py (add a `keychain_secret(service, account=None) -> str | None` helper: macOS `security find-generic-password -s <service> -w` via subprocess, env override `FFS_KEYCHAIN_<SERVICE_UPPER>` for tests, never raises), starter/config/courier.toml and starter/config/sources.toml (new), pyproject.toml only if pytest needs a path. Do NOT touch skills/scribe, crates/, docs/, obsidian-plugin, installer (other forks). Do not commit. TDD. Stdlib only (imaplib, email, html.parser, urllib.request, json, xml.etree, hashlib, tomllib, base64, re, random, time). No em-dashes in prose. No real newsletter or article text: invent publications, headlines, blurbs, and senders in the .eml fixtures; public-record payloads (county permit JSON, Legistar JSON, EDGAR JSON, a press-release RSS) may be realistic but write them yourself as small samples.

The article ingest contract (all four forks code to exactly this; do not deviate): one markdown file per item in `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/`, filename `<publication-slug>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<title-slug>.md` (slug: lowercase, spaces and punctuation to single hyphens, max 80 chars, no trailing hyphen), YAML frontmatter with keys in this order: `predicate: source.article`, `title`, `url` (normalized), `publication`, `published_at` (YYYY-MM-DD), `byline` (omit when unknown), `tags` (flow list, omit when empty), `intake` (`pointer | clip | feed | morning_read`), `reported_by` (omit unless the item attributes another outlet in a trailing parenthetical like "(Charlotte Business Journal)"), `content_hash` (omit unless a feed adapter has the full record bytes; multibase base58btc of blake2b-256 with the `z` prefix computed by the Python side), `fetch` (`off | session | scheduled`, the publisher's policy at the time of filing). Then a blank line and the body: empty for `pointer`; the blurb or article text for `clip`; the record's own summary for `feed`. Then, only when non-empty, `## Mentions` with bullets `- <Name> — <one-line role or org context>` (the separator is a spaced em dash exactly; this is the contract's literal grammar), then optional `## Events` with bullets `- <kind>: <one-line description> | <Name> (<role>), <Name> (<role>)`. For `pointer` items no Mentions section; for `clip` none (the scribe fills from the body); for `feed` items the adapter MAY pre-fill Mentions and adds the tag `courier-structured`. Digest note: one file per publication per day `<publication-slug>-digest-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` with frontmatter `predicate: note`, `title: <Publication> digest YYYY-MM-DD`, `tags: [digest, courier]`, body one line "Filed by the courier.", then `## References` with bullets `- [[<article basename>|<title>]]` where the article basename is the ingest filename stem; a second tick the same day appends new bullets to the existing digest file in ingest/ if it still exists, else writes a new digest note. Tick result JSON (printed and returned to the host): `{ "tick": "mailbox"|"feed:<name>", "dry_run": bool, "items_seen": n, "files_written": n, "files": [paths], "would_submit": [paths] (dry run), "fetch_requests": [{url, status}], "fetch_failures": n, "skipped_seen": n, "warnings": [], "last_error": null|str }`. Vocabulary in messages: submitted, proposed, filed, auto-filed; a courier says "submitted" or, in dry run, "would submit", never "filed". After every real tick write `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/last_run.json` `{last_run (ISO), tick, items_seen, files_written, fetch_failures, last_error}` (the daemon's health.summary reads it). Ledger: `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/seen.json` keyed by normalized url with first-seen date; dedup also consults the substrate via `query("entity.search", {"query": <url>, "predicate": "source.article", "limit": 1})` when the host is present (wrap in try; absent host means ledger only).

Config: `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/courier.toml` per the task's requirement (mailbox host/port/folder/auth app_password|oauth/mark_seen, [[mailbox.source]] sender/subject_filter/publisher, [[feed]] adapter/endpoint or url/since/publication/filters, [edgar] user_agent (required when an edgar feed exists) and max_rps default 8 ceiling 10, [output] digest_title_prefix, [tracking] wrappers: a table of {host_pattern, kind: "base64_path_segment", segment_index} extensible by the owner; the starter file includes the link.bizjournals.com/click wrapper), env overrides FFS_COURIER_* ; any key named password, token, secret, or cookie in the TOML is refused with a clear error; the mailbox password comes from keychain service `ffs.courier.<host>` or env FFS_COURIER_MAIL_PASSWORD; auth = "oauth" is accepted by the loader but the mailbox connect returns a clear "oauth is not implemented in this release; use app_password with a Google Workspace app password (requires 2-step verification)" error. `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/sources.toml`: `[[publisher]]` with key, name, domains (list), intake (pointer|clip), fetch (off|session|scheduled), daily_cap (default 20), min_pause_seconds (default 8); loader validates enums, rejects unknown keys, has NO domain denylist or allowlist anywhere in the bundle (a test greps the bundle for the three publisher domains outside the starter file and fixtures and asserts none in code); starter file: bizjournals.com pointer/session, charlotteobserver.com pointer/session, axios.com pointer/session (comment: terms recorded in docs/research/spikes/task-43-intake-reality.md; the setting is the owner's), clttoday (6amcity.com, clttoday.com) clip/off, and the four feeds' publishers clip/scheduled; a mailbox source whose publisher key is missing files as pointer with a warning.

Mailbox tick: imaplib connect (SSL), select folder, search UNSEEN (or all when mark_seen is false and a since date is given), filter by sender (address or domain) and subject regex, parse each message's HTML (html.parser subclass collecting anchors with text and hrefs, and the text between anchors as blurb candidates) or text part; decode tracking wrappers (base64url path segment, padding fixed) to the real url; normalize; drop links whose host is not in the publisher's domains; keep one item per unique normalized url with the anchor text as headline and, for clip publishers, the nearest following text block as blurb and a trailing "(Outlet)" parenthetical as reported_by; skip items in the ledger or substrate; write files per the contract; write or append the digest; update the ledger; mark seen only if every file was written; second tick over the same message writes zero files. Dry run (FFS_COURIER_DRY_RUN=1 or input {"dry_run": true}) writes to `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/dry-run/<timestamp>/`, no ledger update, no mark-seen, no last_run.json, result lists would_submit. Inject the IMAP client and urllib opener (module-level factory functions) so tests use fakes; provide a FakeImap over .eml files.

Feed adapters (each `tick(cfg, since, fetcher) -> list[Record]` plus `to_ingest(record) -> (filename, text)`): meck_permits (FeatureServer query with where clause on issue date >= since, optional min cost and type; each record becomes an event.business-hinted file: `predicate: event.business` is NOT the contract for feeds; keep the article contract: predicate source.article with intake feed, publication "Mecklenburg County permits", title from project name or permit type + address, url the record's permit url or the query url with the permit id, body the record summary, `## Mentions` with the owner name tagged courier-structured, `## Events` bullet `- <opening|expansion|other>: <description> | <Owner> (developer)` with amount in the description); charlotte_legistar (events and matters since a date; petitioners into Mentions; Events bullet kind other with the meeting date); sec_edgar (full-text search q and forms with the declared User-Agent header and a token-bucket limiter at max_rps, no crawling beyond the query; 8-K item 5.02 records produce a Mentions bullet for the officer with the company as context); rss (RSS 2.0 and Atom via xml.etree; guid dedup; each entry a source.article with intake clip and reported_by = the publisher). Watermark advances only after every file was written. Rate limiter test: never exceeds max_rps.

Scheduled fetch (fetch.py): for each new pointer whose publisher has fetch = "scheduled": cookies from keychain service `ffs.courier.cookies.<domain>` (Netscape cookie-jar text) or env FFS_COURIER_COOKIES_<DOMAIN_UPPER_WITH_UNDERSCORES>; one urllib request per url with a browser-like User-Agent and the cookies, timeout 20 s; randomized pause of at least min_pause_seconds between requests; stop at daily_cap per publisher per day (count in the ledger); request only urls that came from the digest (assert in code: the url must be in this tick's item list); log every request in fetch_requests; on 200 extract the main text (html.parser: title, paragraphs inside <article> or the largest text block), rewrite that item's file as intake clip with content_hash and the body; any other status keeps the pointer and counts fetch_failures. Tests with a stubbed opener: only digest urls requested; pause and cap honored (patch time.sleep and random); 403 keeps pointer; 200 rewrites clip; starter sources.toml never triggers it for the three publishers; a test sources.toml with one of them set to scheduled triggers exactly its digest urls.

Also: skills/_lib/urlnorm.py `normalize_url(raw) -> str` (lowercase scheme and host, strip utm_*/fbclid/gclid/mc_cid/mc_eid params, drop fragment, collapse trailing slash, keep other params sorted? no: keep order, only remove the listed), `article_basename(publication, date, title) -> str`, `content_hash_multibase(bytes) -> str` (blake2b digest_size=32, multibase base58btc 'z' prefix; implement base58 yourself), and the shared fixture skills/_lib/fixtures/urlnorm.json with at least 12 pairs including a wrapper-decoded url; tests. Put the courier's expected outputs for the primary synthetic fixture under skills/courier/tests/fixtures/expected/ (one article file, one digest file) and assert the writer reproduces them byte for byte; the docs fork will embed exactly those files.

Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/` bare (the repo-root conftest layout: give skills/courier/tests/conftest.py its own sys.path setup like the auditor's; there is no tests/__init__.py by design). Report the summary line, the exact tick-result keys, the starter TOML files' contents summary, and the expected-output fixture paths.

Digest note: one file per publication per day `<publication-slug>-digest-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` with frontmatter `predicate: note`, `title: <Publication> digest YYYY-MM-DD`, `tags: [digest, courier]`, body one line "Filed by the courier.", then `## References` with bullets `- [[<article basename>|<title>]]` where the article basename is the ingest filename stem; a second tick the same day appends new bullets to the existing digest file in ingest/ if it still exists, else writes a new digest note. Tick result JSON (printed and returned to the host): `{ "tick": "mailbox"|"feed:<name>", "dry_run": bool, "items_seen": n, "files_written": n, "files": [paths], "would_submit": [paths] (dry run), "fetch_requests": [{url, status}], "fetch_failures": n, "skipped_seen": n, "warnings": [], "last_error": null|str }`. Vocabulary in messages: submitted, proposed, filed, auto-filed; a courier says "submitted" or, in dry run, "would submit", never "filed". After every real tick write `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/last_run.json` `{last_run (ISO), tick, items_seen, files_written, fetch_failures, last_error}` (the daemon's health.summary reads it). Ledger: `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/seen.json` keyed by normalized url with first-seen date; dedup also consults the substrate via `query("entity.search", {"query": <url>, "predicate": "source.article", "limit": 1})` when the host is present (wrap in try; absent host means ledger only).

Config: `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/courier.toml` per the task's requirement (mailbox host/port/folder/auth app_password|oauth/mark_seen, [[mailbox.source]] sender/subject_filter/publisher, [[feed]] adapter/endpoint or url/since/publication/filters, [edgar] user_agent (required when an edgar feed exists) and max_rps default 8 ceiling 10, [output] digest_title_prefix, [tracking] wrappers: a table of {host_pattern, kind: "base64_path_segment", segment_index} extensible by the owner; the starter file includes the link.bizjournals.com/click wrapper), env overrides FFS_COURIER_* ; any key named password, token, secret, or cookie in the TOML is refused with a clear error; the mailbox password comes from keychain service `ffs.courier.<host>` or env FFS_COURIER_MAIL_PASSWORD; auth = "oauth" is accepted by the loader but the mailbox connect returns a clear "oauth is not implemented in this release; use app_password with a Google Workspace app password (requires 2-step verification)" error. `$FFS_DATA_DIR/config/sources.toml`: `[[publisher]]` with key, name, domains (list), intake (pointer|clip), fetch (off|session|scheduled), daily_cap (default 20), min_pause_seconds (default 8); loader validates enums, rejects unknown keys, has NO domain denylist or allowlist anywhere in the bundle (a test greps the bundle for the three publisher domains outside the starter file and fixtures and asserts none in code); starter file: bizjournals.com pointer/session, charlotteobserver.com pointer/session, axios.com pointer/session (comment: terms recorded in docs/research/spikes/task-43-intake-reality.md; the setting is the owner's), clttoday (6amcity.com, clttoday.com) clip/off, and the four feeds' publishers clip/scheduled; a mailbox source whose publisher key is missing files as pointer with a warning.

Mailbox tick: imaplib connect (SSL), select folder, search UNSEEN (or all when mark_seen is false and a since date is given), filter by sender (address or domain) and subject regex, parse each message's HTML (html.parser subclass collecting anchors with text and hrefs, and the text between anchors as blurb candidates) or text part; decode tracking wrappers (base64url path segment, padding fixed) to the real url; normalize; drop links whose host is not in the publisher's domains; keep one item per unique normalized url with the anchor text as headline and, for clip publishers, the nearest following text block as blurb and a trailing "(Outlet)" parenthetical as reported_by; skip items in the ledger or substrate; write files per the contract; write or append the digest; update the ledger; mark seen only if every file was written; second tick over the same message writes zero files. Dry run (FFS_COURIER_DRY_RUN=1 or input {"dry_run": true}) writes to `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/.courier/dry-run/<timestamp>/`, no ledger update, no mark-seen, no last_run.json, result lists would_submit. Inject the IMAP client and urllib opener (module-level factory functions) so tests use fakes; provide a FakeImap over .eml files.

Feed adapters (each `tick(cfg, since, fetcher) -> list[Record]` plus `to_ingest(record) -> (filename, text)`): meck_permits (FeatureServer query with where clause on issue date >= since, optional min cost and type; each record becomes an event.business-hinted file: `predicate: event.business` is NOT the contract for feeds; keep the article contract: predicate source.article with intake feed, publication "Mecklenburg County permits", title from project name or permit type + address, url the record's permit url or the query url with the permit id, body the record summary, `## Mentions` with the owner name tagged courier-structured, `## Events` bullet `- <opening|expansion|other>: <description> | <Owner> (developer)` with amount in the description); charlotte_legistar (events and matters since a date; petitioners into Mentions; Events bullet kind other with the meeting date); sec_edgar (full-text search q and forms with the declared User-Agent header and a token-bucket limiter at max_rps, no crawling beyond the query; 8-K item 5.02 records produce a Mentions bullet for the officer with the company as context); rss (RSS 2.0 and Atom via xml.etree; guid dedup; each entry a source.article with intake clip and reported_by = the publisher). Watermark advances only after every file was written. Rate limiter test: never exceeds max_rps.

Scheduled fetch (fetch.py): for each new pointer whose publisher has fetch = "scheduled": cookies from keychain service `ffs.courier.cookies.<domain>` (Netscape cookie-jar text) or env FFS_COURIER_COOKIES_<DOMAIN_UPPER_WITH_UNDERSCORES>; one urllib request per url with a browser-like User-Agent and the cookies, timeout 20 s; randomized pause of at least min_pause_seconds between requests; stop at daily_cap per publisher per day (count in the ledger); request only urls that came from the digest (assert in code: the url must be in this tick's item list); log every request in fetch_requests; on 200 extract the main text (html.parser: title, paragraphs inside <article> or the largest text block), rewrite that item's file as intake clip with content_hash and the body; any other status keeps the pointer and counts fetch_failures. Tests with a stubbed opener: only digest urls requested; pause and cap honored (patch time.sleep and random); 403 keeps pointer; 200 rewrites clip; starter sources.toml never triggers it for the three publishers; a test sources.toml with one of them set to scheduled triggers exactly its digest urls.

Also: skills/_lib/urlnorm.py `normalize_url(raw) -> str` (lowercase scheme and host, strip utm_*/fbclid/gclid/mc_cid/mc_eid params, drop fragment, collapse trailing slash, keep other params sorted? no: keep order, only remove the listed), `article_basename(publication, date, title) -> str`, `content_hash_multibase(bytes) -> str` (blake2b digest_size=32, multibase base58btc 'z' prefix; implement base58 yourself), and the shared fixture skills/_lib/fixtures/urlnorm.json with at least 12 pairs including a wrapper-decoded url; tests. Put the courier's expected outputs for the primary synthetic fixture under skills/courier/tests/fixtures/expected/ (one article file, one digest file) and assert the writer reproduces them byte for byte; the docs fork will embed exactly those files.

Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/` bare (the repo-root conftest layout: give skills/courier/tests/conftest.py its own sys.path setup like the auditor's; there is no tests/__init__.py by design). Report the summary line, the exact tick-result keys, the starter TOML files' contents summary, and the expected-output fixture paths.

input.prompt:
You own the scribe slice of task_40 (subtask 40.5; read .compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/task_40.md requirements on the contract and the scribe, adr-031, adr-030, and the current skills/scribe/{engine.py,heuristic.py,extraction.py,llm.py,registry.py,validate.py} and tests). Files you own: skills/scribe/** only. Do NOT touch skills/courier, skills/_lib, crates/, docs/ (other forks; skills/_lib/urlnorm.py is being written concurrently by the courier fork: import it lazily with a fallback that leaves urls as-is when the module is absent). Multi-entity wire (already implemented by task_45 in engine.py/llm.py): proposals may carry local_ref, refs [{field, local_ref}], valid_from, valid_to, ends_role, and a source_article provenance entry; cross-references are display strings.

Do, in the frontmatter-hint path (engine.apply_hint / _claim_from_frontmatter) and the heuristic engine so the courier's files work with FFS_SCRIBE_ENGINE=heuristic and no LLM:
1. When the hint is `source.article` (or any registered predicate whose schema has a `mentions` array of objects), parse `## Mentions` bullets into `mentions[]` items `{display, context}` verbatim (no entity key) on the article claim, and additionally emit one secondary proposal per bullet: `person.generic` when the context suggests a person (has a role word, or the display looks like a person name by the existing name heuristics) else `org.company`, with `display_name` = display and, for people, `organization` set to an org display found in the same context or the same set when present, `role` from the context when it is a title; each secondary proposal carries `local_ref`, the source_article provenance entry, and the article's refs binding (`mentions[i].entity` -> that local_ref) so task_45's resolver and accept path rewrite it to an entity id; when the bullet carries a `courier-structured` tag (article tags include courier-structured) set rationale "courier-structured hint" and include the record id from provenance if present. If the registry lacks person.generic or org.company, keep only the article's mentions[] and warn.
2. Parse `## Events` bullets into `event.business` proposals: kind, summary = description, `participants[]` items `{display, role}`, `date` = the article's published_at, `source` = the article url, `title` = the description truncated to 80 chars; participants that match a Mentions display get refs to that local_ref; each carries the source_article provenance.
3. Round-trip frontmatter: `content_hash` into the article claim when the schema declares it; `intake`, `reported_by`, and `fetch` are NOT claim fields: put `reported_by` into a provenance entry `{"kind": "reported_by", "uri": "outlet:<name>", "hash_hex": <content hash>}` and `intake`/`fetch` into the rationale text ("intake: pointer, fetch: session") and as tags `intake-pointer` on the article claim only if the schema has tags (it does). Absent values yield nothing.
4. Body truncation: a configurable limit (env FFS_SCRIBE_BODY_LIMIT, default 4000 chars) applied to any body copied into a claim string field (summary, body, description); when truncated, append "(truncated)" and add a `parse-warning: body truncated from N to M characters` to the proposal's rationale and a warning to the result.
5. Notes: `## References` bullets populate `references[]` (the url for url bullets; the basename for wikilink bullets `[[basename|title]]`; deduped) on note proposals from both the heuristic note path and the frontmatter-hint path, and the digest note (`predicate: note`, title "... digest ...") therefore lands with references.
6. Also in the llm prompt (prompt.py): one sentence telling the model that `## Mentions` and `## Events` sections, when present, are structured hints to honor verbatim for display names and roles (do not hardcode any predicate).

Tests (new test_contract.py or extend test_hint.py): mentions bullets yield {display, context} objects on the article and person/org secondary proposals with refs and source_article provenance; courier-structured hint rationale; events bullets yield event.business with participants roles (unknown role -> other) and refs to mentions; content_hash round-trips, reported_by becomes provenance, intake/fetch never enter the claim; truncation with parse-warning; references populated from wikilink and url bullets on a digest note; a pointer file (empty body, no sections) yields exactly one source.article proposal and nothing else; the whole thing works with the heuristic engine (no FFS_SCRIBE_ENGINE set). Run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/scribe/tests/` and then `.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/` bare; report summary lines and the exact provenance kinds and tag names you emit.

input.prompt:
You own the Rust slice of task_40 (subtasks 40.2 Rust side, 40.6, 40.7, 40.8, 40.9; read .compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/task_40.md in full, adr-030, adr-031, adr-035, and the current crates/ffs-daemon/src/{dispatch.rs,api.rs,resolver.rs,scribe.rs,main.rs}, crates/ffs-core/src/{resolve.rs,store/mod.rs,quarantine.rs}, crates/ffs-mcp/src/tools.rs, crates/ffs-cli/src/{lib.rs,commands.rs}, skills/auditor/audit.py). Files you own: crates/ffs-core/src/urlnorm.rs (new) + lib.rs export, crates/ffs-daemon/src/**, crates/ffs-daemon/tests/**, crates/ffs-mcp/**, crates/ffs-cli/**, skills/auditor/audit.py and its tests (the courier line and flag only), installer/install.sh and install.ps1 (copy skills/courier and seed starter/config/{courier,sources}.toml, following the existing skill copy pattern; the files are being written concurrently, so reference them by path without reading their contents). Do NOT touch skills/courier, skills/scribe, skills/_lib, docs/, obsidian-plugin. Do not commit. TDD. CLAUDE.md rules. No em-dashes in prose.

Shared fixture: the courier fork writes skills/_lib/fixtures/urlnorm.json as a JSON array of {"raw": ..., "normalized": ...}; your Rust test reads it via a path relative to CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and skips with a clear message if the file is absent at test time (it will be present at integration). Normalization rule (identical on both sides): lowercase scheme and host; strip query params named utm_* (prefix), fbclid, gclid, mc_cid, mc_eid, keeping the others in original order; drop the fragment; collapse a trailing slash (but keep a lone "/" path); leave path case as is. `content_hash` accepts multibase strings whose decoded bytes start with the multihash prefixes for blake3-256 (0x1e 0x20) or blake2b-256 (0xb220 varint: bytes 0xa0 0xe4 0x02 0x20) and compares by the full string; expose `fn same_content_hash(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool` and `fn normalize_url(&str) -> String` and `fn article_basename(publication, date, title) -> String` (slug rule: lowercase, runs of non-alphanumerics to single hyphens, trim hyphens, max 80 chars).

input.description: task_40 F4: contract docs + onboarding
input.prompt:
You own the docs slice of task_40 (subtasks 40.1 and 40.10; read .compozy/tasks/ffs-mvp/task_40.md requirements on the contract, the agent-hosted skill, and the first-use guide; adr-035 with its 2026-09-15 amendment; adr-034 on reported_by and source independence; docs/agent-memory/CONVENTION.md, README.md, skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md, skill/ffs-memory/SKILL.md; docs/onboarding/first-use-guide.md). Files you own: docs/agent-memory/CONVENTION.md (new section), docs/agent-memory/README.md, docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md (reframe), docs/onboarding/first-use-guide.md (new section), docs/onboarding/technical-friend-checklist.md (courier setup lines). Do NOT touch skills/, crates/, starter/, installer/. Do not commit. No em-dashes in prose except where quoting the contract's literal bullet separator.

The article ingest contract to publish (fixed; other forks implement exactly this): one markdown file per item in `$FFS_DATA_DIR/ingest/`, filename `<publication-slug>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<title-slug>.md`; frontmatter keys in order: `predicate: source.article`, `title`, `url` (normalized: lowercase scheme and host, utm_*/fbclid/gclid/mc_cid/mc_eid stripped, fragment dropped, trailing slash collapsed), `publication`, `published_at` (YYYY-MM-DD), `byline` (omit if unknown), `tags` (omit if empty), `intake` (`pointer | clip | feed | morning_read`), `reported_by` (omit unless the item attributes another outlet), `content_hash` (omit unless a feed adapter had the record bytes; multibase base58btc of blake2b-256), `fetch` (`off | session | scheduled`, the publisher's policy at filing time); body empty for pointer, the blurb or article text for clip, the record summary for feed, the owner's note for morning_read; clipped bodies land under the `clip` classification tier (never federated unless a capability names the tier); `## Mentions` bullets `- <Name> — <one-line role or org context>` (spaced em dash), each becoming a `mentions[]` item `{entity, display, context}` with `entity` filled by the resolver, never by the courier; optional `## Events` bullets `- <kind>: <description> | <Name> (<role>), <Name> (<role>)` with kinds [funding, acquisition, hire, departure, expansion, opening, closing, award, partnership, other] and roles [acquirer, target, investor, investee, hire, employer, departing, landlord, tenant, developer, winner, partner, other]; pointer items have no Mentions; clip items leave it to the scribe; feed items may pre-fill it tagged `courier-structured`; the scribe truncates bodies over 4,000 characters with a parse-warning. Digest note: `<publication-slug>-digest-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, frontmatter `predicate: note`, `title: <Publication> digest YYYY-MM-DD`, `tags: [digest, courier]`, body "Filed by the courier.", `## References` bullets `- [[<article basename>|<title>]]`. Persistence vocabulary: submitted (file dropped), proposed (in quarantine), filed (accepted atom in the vault), auto-filed (accepted by an ADR-029 policy); a courier says "submitted" or "would submit", never "filed".

Do:
1. CONVENTION.md: a new numbered section "Article intake contract" (place it after the provenance section; renumber the following sections and the summary references if the doc numbers them) stating the contract above, the no-full-text-unless-policy rule (what the owner's `sources.toml` allowed), the `reported_by` independence rule (an item attributed to another outlet counts as a copy of that outlet for ADR-034), and the persistence vocabulary. Also a short paragraph in the Human override or Capability section: publisher fetch and clip policy is the owner's configuration in `sources.toml`; the software records terms and does not adjudicate them (ADR-035 amendment).
2. docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md: reframe as the agent-hosted alternative: an agent host (Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code) may run the same contract as `skills/courier/`; it reads the same `courier.toml` and `sources.toml` and honors them exactly (it does not decide for the owner; a `session` publisher's articles are opened only in the morning read, task_48, with the owner present); the loop: read the digest email, decode tracking links, write one ingest file per item per the contract with intake and fetch from the publisher's entry, write the digest note, then confirm with `ffs_search` (query the url, predicate source.article) or `ffs ls articles/recent/`, and report with the persistence vocabulary; refuse bulk-open or crawl requests as behavior, not by domain. Include the worked example as two fenced blocks embedded by INCLUDING the exact text of the files `skills/courier/tests/fixtures/expected/*.md` that the courier fork is producing concurrently: if those files exist when you write, copy them verbatim; if not, write the blocks with a marker line `<!-- courier-expected-fixture: article -->` and `<!-- courier-expected-fixture: digest -->` inside empty fences and say so in your report so the coordinator can paste them.
3. docs/agent-memory/README.md: list both couriers (bundle at skills/courier/, installed under $FFS_DATA_DIR/skills/courier/; agent-hosted at skill/ffs-courier/) and the morning read (task_48) as the way terms-restricted publishers get read; one paragraph on sources.toml.
4. first-use-guide.md: a "Read the paper for me" section: what goes in courier.toml (mailbox host, folder, sources with sender and publisher) and sources.toml (intake and fetch per publisher, the starter defaults and why: terms recorded in the spike note, the setting is yours), how to put the mailbox app password in the keychain (`security add-generic-password -s ffs.courier.<host> -a ffs -w`), how to export session cookies for a publisher you set to scheduled and store them (`ffs.courier.cookies.<domain>`), which feeds to turn on (county permits and the Council API first), what `ffs courier run --dry-run` prints and where the scratch files go, what a real run puts in the vault (articles/, the digest note, then people/ and orgs/ after review), and what "ambiguous" in the review means. technical-friend-checklist.md: three lines under the daemon setup: seed the two config files, add the keychain secret, run the dry run.

Report the files changed, whether the worked example was embedded or left with markers, and the new section number in CONVENTION.md.

EOF

"""Mecklenburg County permits via the county's ArcGIS FeatureServer
(``AccelaAllPermits``): REST JSON, no key, public record. One query per
tick, filtered by issue date >= since and optional minimum declared
cost and permit type. Each record becomes a ``feed`` item whose
``## Mentions`` carries the owner (courier-structured) and whose
``## Events`` bullet names the owner as developer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, List
from urllib.parse import urlencode

from . import Fetcher, fetch_json
from writer import Item

DEFAULT_ENDPOINT = (
    "https://meckgis.mecklenburgcountync.gov/server/rest/services/AccelaAllPermits/FeatureServer/0/query"
)
PUBLICATION = "Mecklenburg County permits"


def _epoch_ms_to_date(v: Any) -> str:
    try:
        return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(v) / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError):
        return ""


def query_url(feed_endpoint: str, since: str, filters: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    where = [f"ISSUEDDATE >= DATE '{since}'"] if since else ["1=1"]
    if filters.get("min_cost"):
        where.append(f"DECLAREDVALUE >= {float(filters['min_cost'])}")
    if filters.get("permit_type"):
        where.append("PERMITTYPE = '" + str(filters["permit_type"]).replace("'", "''") + "'")
    params = {
        "where": " AND ".join(where),
        "outFields": "*",
        "orderByFields": "ISSUEDDATE DESC",
        "resultRecordCount": str(int(filters.get("max_records", 200))),
        "f": "json",
    }
    return (feed_endpoint or DEFAULT_ENDPOINT) + "?" + urlencode(params)


def tick(feed: Any, since: str, fetcher: Fetcher, ctx: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    url = query_url(feed.endpoint, since, feed.filters)
    data = fetch_json(fetcher, url, {"Accept": "application/json"})
    records: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for f in data.get("features", []) or []:
        a = f.get("attributes") or {}
        # A row without a permit number is not a permit record (a sign
        # or a placeholder feature); skip it rather than inventing an id.
        pid = str(a.get("PERMITNUMBER") or "").strip()
        if not pid:
            continue
        date = _epoch_ms_to_date(a.get("ISSUEDDATE")) or since
        owner = str(a.get("OWNERNAME") or a.get("APPLICANT") or "").strip()
        project = str(a.get("PROJECTNAME") or "").strip()
        ptype = str(a.get("PERMITTYPE") or "permit").strip()
        addr = str(a.get("ADDRESS") or "").strip()
        cost = a.get("DECLAREDVALUE")
        title = project or f"{ptype} at {addr}" if addr else (project or ptype)
        summary_bits = [f"Permit {pid}", ptype]
        if addr:
            summary_bits.append(addr)
        if cost:
            summary_bits.append(f"declared value ${float(cost):,.0f}")
        if owner:
            summary_bits.append(f"owner {owner}")
        records.append(
            {
                "id": pid,
                "date": date,
                "title": title,
                "url": (feed.endpoint or DEFAULT_ENDPOINT).rsplit("/query", 1)[0] + f"?permit={pid}",
                "summary": "; ".join(summary_bits) + ".",
                "owner": owner,
                "kind": "opening" if "new" in ptype.lower() else ("expansion" if "addition" in ptype.lower() or "alteration" in ptype.lower() else "other"),
                "amount": cost,
                "raw": a,
            }
        )
    return records


def to_item(rec: Dict[str, Any], feed: Any, fetch_policy: str) -> Item:
    mentions = [(rec["owner"], f"permit owner, {rec['title']}")] if rec.get("owner") else []
    desc = rec["summary"].rstrip(".")
    events = [(rec["kind"], desc, [(rec["owner"], "developer")] if rec.get("owner") else [])]
    return Item(
        title=rec["title"],
        url=rec["url"],
        publication=feed.publication or PUBLICATION,
        published_at=rec["date"],
        intake="feed",
        fetch=fetch_policy,
        body=rec["summary"],
        tags=["courier-structured", "permit"],
        mentions=mentions,
        events=events,
    )

    # Filter by date and type on the server, by cost on the client.
    where = [f"issue_date >= DATE '{since}'"] if since else ["1=1"]
    if filters.get("permit_type"):
        where.append("permit_type = '" + str(filters["permit_type"]).replace("'", "''") + "'")
    params = {
        "where": " AND ".join(where),

        if min_cost and cost < min_cost:
            continue
        date = _epoch_ms_to_date(a.get("issue_date")) or since
        owner = str(a.get("owner_name") or "").strip()
        project = str(a.get("project_name") or "").strip()

                "owner": owner,
                "kind": kind,
                "amount": cost or None,
                "raw": a,

What the courier does:
17	
18	- **The owner's own mailbox.** Under the starter defaults the Charlotte Business Journal digest is decoded into `source.article` pointers: title, url (recovered from the base64 path of each `link.bizjournals.com/click/...` tracking link, no click), date, publication, no content. CLTtoday items (6AM City, personal-use license; `intake = "clip"`, `fetch = "off"` because the blurb is the body) are filed with their blurb text and the parenthetical attribution each item carries ("(Charlotte Business Journal)", "(WBTV)"), which goes into provenance as `reported_by` so ADR-034's quorum can discount an item that is itself a copy of another outlet's report. The mailbox is a Google Workspace account; 40.3 decides OAuth versus an app password, with the secret in the OS keychain either way.
19	- **Public-record and permitted feeds**, found by the task_43 probe: the Mecklenburg County permits ArcGIS FeatureServer (`AccelaAllPermits`, REST JSON, no key), the Charlotte City Council Legistar Web API (JSON, no token, 1,000-row cap), SEC EDGAR full-text search and submissions (declared `User-Agent`, 10 requests per second ceiling, no crawling), and newsroom RSS (Duke Energy, Truist). Each is an adapter that writes ingest files under the same contract.
20	
21	An LLM is not needed to move text from an email or a JSON feed into a folder; extraction is the scribe's job (task_36), identity is the resolver's (task_45). So the courier is an FFS skill bundle, `skills/courier/`, the fourth agent ADR-009 named. 22	
23	An agent host (Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code) may run the same contract: `docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-courier/SKILL.md` stays as that statement and a worked example, nothing more. 24	
25	Three gaps this task closes are unchanged from the original scope. There is no published ingest shape for an article, so the scribe guesses from free text and the engines have no stable `predicate:` hint or `## Mentions` section to do multi-entity extraction reliably. Nothing deduplicates by URL, so a re-read files a second article. # Task 48: Morning read: the owner-present reading session skill (ADR-035)

## Overview
ADR-035 splits the newspaper goal in two. The courier (task_40) is deterministic and files pointers and permitted feeds on a schedule. The morning read is the other half: an interactive session in which the owner is present, invokes the read, and works through the day's agenda with an assistant at human pace. The assistant opens one article at a time in the owner's own signed-in browser when the owner says so, summarizes it in the session, proposes the people, organizations, affiliations, and events worth remembering, and files only what the owner chooses, as the owner's own note. Article text is stored only when the owner says "clip this": then the article is filed as a `source.article` with its body under the `clip` classification tier (local library, never federated unless a capability names the tier), with `morning_read` provenance and an attestation (ADR-035 amendment, 2026-09-15). Because the owner decides live, filing from the read is the owner's accept, and each accept emits an ADR-034 attestation.

Publisher policy is the owner's `sources.toml` (task_40). A publisher with `fetch = "session"` is fetched only during the read and only on the owner's cue; the read is the one place such a publisher is opened by the assistant. A publisher with `fetch = "off"` is never fetched by the assistant; the owner opens it and pastes what matters. The read's refusals are behavioral (bulk, prefetch, crawling), never about a domain.

This task delivers that session as an instructional skill for Claude Code (with Claude in Chrome) and for claw hosts with a browser tool, in the same shape as `docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-memory/SKILL.md`. It also settles whether the read needs any new MCP surface. The preference is none: `ffs_author_atom` submits, the existing `ingest.accept` RPC accepts, and task_46's attestation is emitted on accept. If the owner-present accept needs a flag the tools do not carry, that flag is the only addition.

The read doubles as the review. ADR-032's inbox file (accepted 2026-09-20; or `ingest.list_pending` where the inbox is not yet built) is the agenda, and its source order is the read's order: each source's derived proposals (record, people, organizations, affiliations, events, ambiguous resolutions, role changes) are decided together, and "accept all under this article" is the per-source affirmation the owner may give aloud. The agenda items are: courier pointers, CLTtoday extractions, permit and Council items, ambiguous resolutions, and role changes are walked in the same sitting.

The skill MUST say that publisher policy is the owner's `sources.toml` and that the assistant honors `fetch = "session"` (open only in the read, on cue) and `fetch = "off"` (never open; the owner opens and pastes).
- MUST describe the session workflow: (1) open the day's agenda from ADR-032's `inbox/<date>.md` when it exists, else from `ingest.list_pending` via the daemon, walking it in the file's source order so that one article's pointer, extractions, ambiguous resolutions, and role changes are handled together, and speaking every candidate for an ambiguous item aloud rather than only the first (spike 44 showed the owner picks the first-listed candidate); # Task 39: Auto-file policy — `Accept` capability action + additive/conflict routing in the quarantine (ADR-029)

## Overview
The morning-newspaper goal produces 30–60 quarantine proposals a day. Clicking accept on each one is not "keeping the cabinet up to date"; it is the clerk's job done by hand. But the quarantine is the AARM Approval Service and ARCHITECTURE.md names batch approval as an anti-pattern, so the fix cannot be a button. ADR-029 records the decision: a new capability action `Accept`, granted as an ordinary `capability.grant` atom to a specific agent identity and scoped to predicates, plus an **additive rule** enforced by the substrate — auto-accept fires only for proposals that create a new entity, append to a spec-declared additive section, or add an append-only record (`source.article`, `event.business`); any proposal that would supersede an existing scalar field, that the scribe tagged `conflicts`, or that targets a multi-leaf entity always routes to review. Auto-accepted atoms carry the authorizing capability hash in provenance; the daily summary lists what was filed with per-item undo via a new `ingest.retract`; a fresh substrate has no grant (default off).

Amended 2026-09-14 (ADR-030). The entity-identity research (`docs/research/2026-09-14-entity-resolution.md`) made the quarantine the Fellegi-Sunter review band: task_36's resolver now emits `resolution: existing | new | ambiguous` with a `candidates[]` list. This task treats `ambiguous` as always conflicting, renders the review card for it as a reconciliation picker, appends the mention text to the chosen entity's aliases on accept, writes `entity.different_from` only on an explicit owner click, and adds a "Merge into..." action that writes `entity.same_as` with undo by supersession.

Amended 2026-09-14 (ADR-032 proposed, spike task_44) and 2026-09-20 (ADR-032 accepted: inbox file ordered by source, panel counts and link only; `max_per_day` default 50). The review surface is no longer conditional. ADR-032 proposes that the quarantine is also a projection, `inbox/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, with the decisions this task introduces (accept, reject, the reconciliation picker, merge, keep separate, undo) as checkbox lines the fast path parses. Spike task_44 puts one realistic morning in front of the owner in both shapes and decides. The requirements below carry the accepted branch; the daemon-side work (classifier, `Accept` action, RPCs, CLI) is identical either way. The resolver this task consumes now lives in task_45 (split out of task_36), and the `max_per_day` default is 50 from the spike.

<critical>
- ALWAYS READ the PRD and TechSpec before starting
- REFERENCE TECHSPEC for implementation details — do not duplicate here
- FOCUS ON "WHAT" — describe what needs to be accomplished, not how
- MINIMIZE CODE — show code only to illustrate current structure or problem areas
- TESTS REQUIRED — every task MUST include tests in deliverables
</critical>

<requirements>
- MUST add `Action::Accept` (serialized `"accept"`) to `ffs_core::capability::Action` and make `CapabilityClaim` deserialization tolerate unknown action strings (skip, do not fail) so peers on older versions can pull grants they do not understand. Evaluator tests MUST cover: a grant with `actions: ["accept"]` and matching predicate scope → `Allow`; predicate scope mismatch → `Deny`; a superseded grant → `Deny`; `as_of` outside the bitemporal window → `Deny`; a grant carrying only `Write` → `Deny` for `Accept`.
- MUST add `max_per_day: Option<u32>` to `CapabilityScope` (`serde(default)`, omitted when `None`). `narrows_or_equals` MUST treat a smaller-or-equal cap as narrowing and `None` (unlimited) as broader than any `Some`. Usage MUST be counted from the store (atoms with an `auto_accept` provenance entry whose hash equals the grant's hash, `tx_time` within the current UTC day), not from process memory, so the cap survives daemon restarts.
- MUST implement the additive/conflict classifier in `ffs-core::quarantine` as a pure function `classify(proposal, heads, spec) -> Filing::{Additive, Conflicting(reason)}` per ADR-029 § Decision (2). It MUST consult `spec.rendering.additive_sections`, a new optional `[quarantine] append_only = true` spec field (parsed by the predicate loader; ADR-021 extension), the scribe's `resolution` tag from task_36, and multi-leaf head state. Property tests MUST establish: a proposal setting any field that already has a scalar value on a head atom is never `Additive`; a proposal that only appends to `additive_sections` is `Additive` for every generated head state; an append-only predicate's proposal is `Additive` regardless of existing records; a proposal whose resolver candidates include a different `organization` at the same name is `Conflicting`.
- MUST treat `resolution: "ambiguous"` as `Conflicting` unconditionally (amended 2026-09-14, ADR-030): no `Accept` grant, cap, or predicate scope can auto-file an ambiguous proposal. The classifier consumes `resolution` and `candidates[]` from task_36; a proposal with `resolution: "existing"` is classified against that entity's heads, a proposal with `resolution: "new"` is classified as a new entity (additive when the predicate allows).
- MUST render the review card for an ambiguous proposal as a reconciliation picker (amended 2026-09-14, ADR-030): the candidates with their score and `matched_on` evidence (`display_name`, `alias`, `context`) and a one-line summary of each candidate's head (organization, role), a "someone new" option that accepts the proposal as a new entity, and a "these are different people" button that writes an `entity.different_from` atom between the proposal's chosen entity and the rejected candidate. Picking one candidate over another MUST NOT write `different_from`; only the explicit button does.
- MUST append the mention text to the chosen entity's `aliases[]` (amended 2026-09-14, ADR-030) whenever an accepted or auto-accepted proposal resolved to an existing entity and its mention text differs from that entity's `display_name`. The append is an additive-section edit through the same signing path, carries the accepting submission in provenance, and is itself eligible for auto-filing.
- MUST add a "Merge into..." action on person and org cards (amended 2026-09-14, ADR-030) that writes an `entity.same_as` atom (entity = the losing id, claim `{target, reason, criterion}`, owner-signed) via a new `entity.merge { source, target, reason, criterion }` daemon method, and an undo that supersedes the `same_as` atom with `valid_to = now` via `entity.unmerge { same_as_hash }`. The losing entity's atoms MUST stay in place; the materializer renders its projection as a single `Merged into [[...]]` line and the winner's projection includes the losing entity's atoms. `ingest.list_auto_filed` MUST also list merges and unmerges so the daily summary can show them.
- MUST wire auto-accept into the ingest pipeline at the point `quarantine.complete` attaches proposals: resolve the grantee identity from the submission's `source_uri` / provenance (never from content), evaluate `Accept` per proposal target, classify, and sign additive proposals through **the same signing + insert + `AtomCommitted` path as `ingest.accept`** (single writer; materializer renders the file). Conflicting proposals MUST remain `Extracted` and appear in `ingest.list_pending` unchanged. A submission with a mix of additive and conflicting proposals MUST auto-file the additive ones and leave the rest pending, with the submission status reflecting the partial state.
- MUST add `SubmissionStatus::AutoAccepted` (and a partial state for mixed submissions) to the quarantine trait and both backends (in-memory + SQLite, task_29 tables), populating `accepted_atom_hashes`. Existing `ingest.list_pending` semantics MUST NOT change.
- MUST stamp every auto-accepted atom with a provenance entry `{ kind: auto_accept, uri: ffs://local/atom/<capability-hash>, hash: <capability-hash> }` in addition to the proposal's own provenance. `SourceKind` gains `AutoAccept` and `Retraction`.
- MUST add `ingest.list_auto_filed { since? }` returning auto-accepted atoms (hash, entity, predicate, source_uri, tx_time) newest first, and `ingest.retract { atom_hash }` which supersedes the target with a copy carrying `valid_to = now` and provenance `kind: retraction`. `ingest.retract` MUST require the owner's `Supersede` capability on the target and MUST refuse atoms that are not heads. Nothing is erased.
- MUST extend the auditor daily summary (`skills/auditor/audit.py` + `health.summary`) with an `auto_filed` claim section: count for the window, per-predicate counts, and the item list. The panel's five-item cap applies to flags only, not to this list.
- MUST implement the review surface per ADR-032 as accepted 2026-09-20: the inbox file `inbox/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, sections ordered by SOURCE (one per article or feed item, headed by the source title, url, and provenance) with every proposal derived from that source nested under it (the article record, people, organizations, affiliations, events, ambiguous resolutions, role changes), each with its own checkbox block; a per-source `accept all under this article` checkbox that expands to the individual accepts and is refused with a parse warning if an ambiguous section under it has no candidate pick; a final Housekeeping section for cross-source items (merge suggestions, past-window attestations, parse warnings); the "Auto-filed today" list with per-item undo, the reconciliation picker for `ambiguous` proposals, the "Merge into..." and "keep separate" actions, and the retract undo all as rendered sections and checkbox lines per ADR-032 § Decision (1) to (3) and the Amendment; the daemon materializes and re-materializes the file through the suppression registry; the fast path gains the `inbox_decision` reverse-map edit kind whose parser accepts `[x]`, `[X]`, and any non-space character inside the brackets, matches candidate lines on the comment-carried ids, and turns ticks into `ingest.accept` (with `resolved_entity` for candidate lines), `ingest.reject`, `entity.assert_different`, `entity.merge`, and `ingest.retract`, routing contradictory or malformed blocks to a parse warning rendered under the section and surfaced in the panel; the Obsidian summary panel shows only a count line ("N pending, M need your eye") and a link to today's inbox. vitest covers the plugin model and the Obsidian-runtime wrapper stays in `main.ts` per CLAUDE.md.
- MUST set the default `max_per_day` printed in `ffs capability grant --help` and used by the first-use guide's example to 50, spike task_44's finding (46 decisions in 7 minutes on 2026-09-20), so that auto-filed plus inbox items add up to a morning the owner will do.
- MUST add a `capability` CLI subcommand: `ffs capability grant --action <read|write|supersede|accept|…> --grantee <identity> --predicates a,b [--classifications …] [--max-per-day N | --unlimited] [--valid-to …]`, `ffs capability list` (active grants, cap, today's usage), `ffs capability revoke <grant-hash>` (authors a superseding capability with an empty action list). `grant --action accept` without `--max-per-day` or `--unlimited` MUST refuse with a usage error. Backed by new daemon methods `capability.grant`, `capability.list`, `capability.revoke` (owner-signed; the CLI never holds the key).
- MUST default off: no `Accept` grant on a fresh substrate; the owner self-grant bootstrapped on first boot (commit `d1b51e0`) MUST NOT include `accept`.
- MUST document: `docs/onboarding/first-use-guide.md` gains "Letting the clerk file for you" (what auto-files, what never does, how to undo, how to turn it off); `docs/onboarding/troubleshooting.md` gains "Why did this get filed automatically?" (read the `auto_accept` provenance, `ffs capability list`, `ingest.retract`); `docs/agent-memory/CONVENTION.md` § 16 (Human override; renumbered 2026-09-20) gains a sentence that auto-filing is the owner's grant, not the agent's decision.
- MUST NOT change the `ffs_author_atom` MCP signature or the `ingest.accept` / `ingest.reject` semantics.
</requirements>

## Subtasks
- [ ] 39.1 `Action::Accept` + unknown-action-tolerant deserialization; `CapabilityScope.max_per_day` with `narrows_or_equals` semantics; evaluator + scope unit tests (`crates/ffs-core/src/capability/`).
- [ ] 39.2 Predicate loader: optional `[quarantine] append_only` field (`crates/ffs-core/src/predicate/mod.rs`); starter specs for `source.article` and `event.business` (from task_38) set it.
- [ ] 39.3 Classifier `classify(proposal, heads, spec) -> Filing` in `crates/ffs-core/src/quarantine.rs` with proptest coverage; `SourceKind::{AutoAccept, Retraction}`; new submission statuses in both quarantine backends + migration in `quarantine_sqlite.rs`.
- [ ] 39.4 Dispatcher wiring: grantee resolution from `source_uri` / provenance; `Accept` evaluation + classification on `quarantine.complete`; shared `sign_and_insert` helper extracted from `ingest_accept`; `max_per_day` counting from the store; `ingest.list_auto_filed`; `ingest.retract` (`crates/ffs-daemon/src/dispatch.rs`, `api.rs`).
- [ ] 39.5 `capability.grant` / `capability.list` / `capability.revoke` daemon methods; `ffs capability` CLI subcommand (`crates/ffs-cli/src/lib.rs`, `commands.rs`); refuse `accept` without a cap.
- [ ] 39.6 Auditor `auto_filed` section in `health.summary` and `audit.py`; plugin "Auto-filed today" section with undo (`summary.ts`, `main.ts`) + vitest.
- [ ] 39.7 Docs: first-use guide, troubleshooting, CONVENTION.md § 15 sentence; `docs/agent-memory/skill/ffs-memory/SKILL.md` notes that a `submission_id` may resolve to auto-filed atoms and how to check (`ingest.list_auto_filed` is not an MCP tool; the agent still reports "proposed").
- [ ] 39.8 Live validation on the project lead's Mac: grant `accept` for `source.article,event.business,org.company,person.generic` with `--max-per-day 50`; drop a fresh-company article → org file appears in the vault with no click; drop a role change for an existing person → review card, head unchanged; undo one auto-filed atom → file reverts; revoke → next drop is pending only.
- [ ] 39.9 Reconciliation picker (amended 2026-09-14, ADR-030): classifier treats `ambiguous` as `Conflicting`; `ingest.accept` gains an optional `resolved_entity` argument (an existing id or `"new"`) for ambiguous proposals; plugin card renders candidates with score, `matched_on`, and head summary, plus "someone new" and "these are different people"; the latter calls a new `entity.assert_different { a, b, criterion }` daemon method that authors an owner-signed `entity.different_from` atom; alias growth on accept through the shared signing path (`summary.ts`, `main.ts`, `dispatch.rs`, `api.rs`) + vitest.
